docs.title: Example
docs.text: 1979 New spelling Meaning Tyuaa cuaa the child Söèi sɔɛi the word Nyèi ɲɛi the thing Hangullo hangullo the heat Yöngu ndu yɔngu ndu give him Nhömpum ŋɔmpum six Lènnden lɛŋnden the country

docs.title: Punctuation
docs.text:
Punctuation follows the rules of French. The Bible (BKG) uses:

Sign Use Example . end of sentence Mí ɲɔɔ tosan lende. “And it was so.” Gen 1:9 , between clauses, in lists Sɛm, Ham a Yafɛt “Shem, Ham and Japheth” : before reported speech, a list Mí Hala dimi aa: «…» ? question Kuɛɛ nɛ n co yɛ? “Where are you?” Gen 3:9 ! exclamation, command Má cè laa nɔm! “Here is your wife!” Gen 12:19 « » reported speech Mó dimi aa: «Diomndo ndu.» ‹ › speech reported within other speech Gen 3:3 ( ) clarification, aside

docs.title: Reported speech
docs.text:
Direct speech is introduced by the verb of speaking followed by aa “that, this” and a colon, then placed in French quotation marks (guillemets):

Mí Hala dimi aa: «Ɲɔ́ɔ́ téngá!» Mí ɲɔɔ tèngà. “God said, ‘Let there be light!’ And there was light.” Gen 1:3

Rule

  • Quotation marks are written « » (and ‹ › inside), with no space inside the quotation marks in the Bible: «Diomndo ndu.».
  • The final full stop of the speech goes before the closing quotation mark when the quotation is a complete sentence.

Spaces

French typography puts a space before : ; ? !; the Kisiei Bible does not (dimi aa:, yɛ?). This guide follows the Bible. Both practices are readable; what matters is to be consistent within a text.

docs.title: Capitals
docs.text:
Use a capital letter:

  • at the beginning of a sentence: Mí Hala dimi aa…;
  • for proper names of people, places and peoples: Abraham, Esipte “Egypt”, Yerusalɛm, Israɛlla “the Israelites”;
  • for the names of God: Hala “God”, Mɛlɛka “the Lord”.

The letters specific to Kisiei have capitals: Ɛ, Ɔ, Ŋ, Ɲ (Ɲumma, Ɔ̀ɔ́). Titles and headings in the Bible are sometimes written entirely in capitals (KANDƆNNDO).

When a proper name takes a referent with a hyphen, only the first part takes a capital: Hala-o, Aarɔn-nda.

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text: Numbers are normally written in words in running text (pilɛ, tiɔn, kɛmɛ); figures are used for numbering (chapters, verses, dates). See Numerals.

docs.title: A tone language
docs.text:
Kisiei is a tone language: the pitch of the voice on a syllable can change the meaning of a word or the grammatical value of a form. Two levels are distinguished, high and low, which can combine on a long syllable into high-falling and low-rising (Keita 1979, p. 17-18); Southern Kissi has the same inventory (Childs 1995, p. 43). Here are some minimal pairs (respelled forms):

Tone Word Meaning Tone Word Meaning high-fall. kɔɔ kind of snake ≠ low-rise. kɔɔ back low-rise. baa hand ≠ high-fall. baa price low-rise. bɔlɔɔ banana ≠ high-fall. bɔlɔɔ bag

Tone is also used in conjugation: i kela “I walk about (usually)” and i kela “I walked about” differ only in tone (Keita 1979, p. 18) (see Tense, aspect and mood).

docs.title: How the Bible marks tones
docs.text:
The old spelling marked no tones. The Bible (BKG) marks tone with accents:

  • the acute accent ( ´ ) for high tone: mí, náŋ;
  • the grave accent ( ` ) for low tone: mì, nàà;
  • on a long vowel, one accent per vowel: ndóò (high-low), màá (low-high), háá (high-high).

But it does not mark them everywhere: about one word in ten carries an accent. The accents are concentrated on two kinds of words.

docs.title: 1. Grammatical words whose tone changes their function
docs.text:
These are mainly the small words that link clauses. Their tone is always marked:

High tone Use Low tone Use mí “and (then)”, past narrative: Mí Hala dimi aa “And God said” Gen 1:3 mì “and (that)”, intended or future sequence: mì kɔngɔ vesɛiyo lo “and let the dry land appear” Gen 1:9 mó the same, + o “he, she”: mó sɛi “and he separated” Gen 1:4 mò the same, + o: mò vel naa “that he may resemble us” Gen 1:26 má the same, + a “they”: má kɔa yondoo nin “and they went into the bush” Gen 4:8 mà the same, + a: mà va kelaa “that they may fly” Gen 1:20

Other small words always carry their tone: háá “until” (to be distinguished from haa “these”), ndóò (past auxiliary, see Tense), ndáà “them” (beside ndaa “their”), tùú in le tùú “because”, tɔ̀a “all”.

docs.title: 2. Words that would be confused without an accent
docs.text: Some words carry an accent in almost all their occurrences, because they have a homograph: sálà “offering”, lasálàá “sacrifice”, siòònde “fear”, dɔ́ɔ́ngɔ́ “tent”, hɔ́ɔ́yɛi “freedom”.

docs.title: Other words
docs.text:
Common nouns, verbs and adjectives carry no accent: pɔmbɔɔ, cɛiyo, tosa, naŋ. When the same word appears in the Bible both with and without an accent, the form without an accent is generally by far the more frequent (naŋ rather than náŋ). In Southern Kissi, most nouns have only low tones, and the tone of verbs is set by the conjugation rather than by the word itself (Childs 1995, p. 54-55).

Practical rule

  1. Always mark the tone on mí/mì, mó/mò, má/mà and on the small words in the list above.
  2. Mark the tone on a content word only if it could be confused with another word in the context, and then follow the Bible's form.
  3. In all other cases, do not write an accent.
  4. One accent per vowel: a long vowel gets two (ndóò, háá).

Note

The exact tone rules of Kisiei (basic tones of words, tone changes in the sentence) are described neither in the 1979 manual nor in the Bible. They are among the open questions. For Southern Kissi they are described in detail (Childs 1995, p. 43-65, 91-98), but it is not yet known which of them also hold for Kisiei.

docs.title: Intonation
docs.text:
The sentence also has an intonation (Keita 1979, p. 17): a question ends with a rise in the voice, a statement with a fall. In writing, this is shown simply by the question mark or the full stop: A hin? “Are you coming?”, I hin. “I am coming.”

In Southern Kissi, only the closed question (answer yes or no) ends with a rise; a question with a question word ends, like a statement, with a fall (Childs 1995, p. 60-61, 264).

docs.title: The seven vowels
docs.text:
Kisiei has seven vowels, like Southern Kissi (Childs 1995, p. 35). Two of them are written with letters that are not part of the English alphabet.

Letter Pronunciation Example Meaning i i of machine pilɛ one e close e, like ay in say but without the glide towards ee pelei foot ɛ open e, as in bed lɛŋ ground, earth a a of father bala hands ɔ open o, as in law (British thought) pɔmbɔɔ small, younger o close o, like o in go but without the glide towards oo yondoo bush u oo of food cuaa child front back close close-mid open-mid open i u e o ɛ ɔ a The seven vowels by tongue position (front or back, more or less open). Each can be long (doubled letter).

English speakers should keep every vowel pure: Kisiei e and o do not glide like English say and go.

Rule

Always distinguish e / ɛ and o / ɔ: they are different vowels, which change the meaning of words. Do not write é, è or ö: the è and ö of the old spelling become ɛ and ɔ (see From the old to the new spelling).

docs.title: Long vowels
docs.text:
A long vowel is pronounced for longer than a short vowel; it is written by doubling the letter: aa, ee, ɛɛ, ii, oo, ɔɔ, uu. Length changes the meaning of a word (Childs 1995, p. 37-38); it is the most frequent source of errors among learners (Keita 1979, p. 12).

Short Meaning Long Meaning velu beget veelu call yema sister yeema want bala hands baala work koma then, again kooma blood

Examples from the Bible: Mɛɛ Adam velu Sɛt “when Adam begat Seth” Gen 5:4; Mí Mɛlɛka Hala veelu vanapɔnɔɔ “The Lord God called the man” Gen 3:9.

docs.title: Final long vowel and the full form
docs.text:
Very often, the long vowel at the end of a word is not part of the stem: it is the class suffix of a noun or the infinitive marker of a verb. It disappears when the word takes its stem form:

Stem form Full form kala ndɔ “his/her mother” kalaa “the mother” fula “go out (he goes out)” fulaa “to go out, the going out” dio “eat (he eats)” dioo “to eat, the eating”

So do not “correct” kala ndɔ to kalaa ndɔ: the short form is the right one before a determiner (see Word division and Noun classes).

docs.title: Vowel sequences
docs.text:
Two different vowels can follow each other; they are written as they are heard, without a diaeresis or apostrophe:

  • ia, io, iɔ, iɛ: fuɲaa, dioo, tiɔn, ciɛɔn;
  • ua, uɛ, ui: cuaa, ŋuɛɛnu, kuí;
  • ɛi, ei, oi: cɛiyo, pelei, hoeiye.

These sequences are described in 1979 as diphthongs and triphthongs (Keita 1979, p. 11). In Southern Kissi, i and u before another vowel are pronounced as the semivowels [j] and [w], while sequences ending in i or u (ei, ɛi, oi, au…) have the length of a long vowel (Childs 1995, p. 39-42). The Bible (BKG) always writes them with the ordinary letters.

docs.title: Nasal vowels
docs.text:
When a vowel is followed by n at the end of a syllable, it is pronounced nasalised: an, ɛn, in, on, ɔn, un. No sign is added; simply write the vowel followed by n:

diolan “name”, mɛnndan “water”, nin “in”, kon “that…”, sɔɔn “words”, hun “come”.

In Southern Kissi, this final nasal is analysed as a consonant [ŋ] that nasalises the preceding vowel; it would continue earlier nasal vowels (Childs 1995, p. 88-89).

Note

At the end of a stem, the nasal sound can be [n] or [ŋ], and the Bible distinguishes them: nan “pull” (má nan Yosɛf “they pulled Joseph” Gen 37:28) is not naŋ “good”. See Consonants.

The sequences am, om, im… are not nasal vowels, but a vowel followed by the consonant m (Keita 1979, p. 13): yɔmndo is divided yɔm-ndo.

docs.title: Word division and the hyphen
docs.text: Knowing where a word begins and ends is one of the main difficulties in writing Kisiei. This chapter brings together the rules followed by the Bible (BKG).

docs.title: Full form and stem form of the noun
docs.text:
A noun has two written forms (see Noun classes):

  • the full form, with its class suffix, when the noun stands alone or at the end of a phrase: cɛiyo “the house”, yɔmndo “the tree”, diolan “the name”;
  • the stem form, without a suffix, when the noun is followed by a determiner, an adjective, a number or a possessor: cɛi kon “that house”, yɔm kon “that tree”, diola ndɔlan “his/her name”.

Rule

The stem form is a separate word, separated by a space from what follows. Do not write cɛikon or cɛi-kon.

Southern Kissi has the same alternation: the noun's suffix moves onto the word that modifies it (Childs 1995, p. 150-151).

docs.title: Grammatical words are written separately
docs.text:
Pronouns, auxiliaries, prepositions, demonstratives and possessives are written as separate words:

O co kɛndia le “he (she) is not well” 1 Sam 19:14 — o “he, she”, co “be”, kɛndia “in good health”, le (negation).

Mí Hala ca maa ɲɛ-tengaa naŋ “And God saw that the light was good” Gen 1:4.

The final negation le / te is also a separate word; write te after n, m, ŋ or l, and le after a vowel or w (see Negation; in Southern Kissi, te follows any consonant (Childs 1995, p. 89, 125)): La kei nanu le “do not pass through here” Num 20:20, Vana diinin nɔm te “no one will kill you” 2 Sam 19:24.

docs.title: The hyphen
docs.text: The Bible uses the hyphen a great deal (nearly 18,000 times). It has three uses.

docs.title: 1. The referent that closes a phrase
docs.text:
When a noun phrase ends with something other than the noun itself — a relative clause, a complement, a proper name — the noun's class is repeated by a referent (a class marker) which is attached by a hyphen to the last word of the phrase:

Group Referent Example class o (singular) -o, -ndo, -yo, -lo kɔngɔ vesɛi fula-o “the dry land that appeared” Gen 1:10 Kɔl Hala-o “the Spirit of God” Gen 1:2 o co paalen-ndo “the one that is the sun” Gen 1:16 class a (plural, persons) -a, -nda visia pɔmbɔa kela lɛŋ-nda “the small animals that walk on the ground” Gen 1:24 class an -an mɛmma co lebɛngu-an “the waters that are below” Gen 1:7 class e / i -e, -nde sɔɛi Mɛlɛka dimul ndu-e “the word that the Lord had spoken to him” Gen 15:6

The choice between -o, -ndo, -yo or -lo (and likewise -a / -nda, -e / -nde) depends on the end of the word to which the referent is attached: after a nasal write -ndo, -nda, -nde (lɛŋnden-ndo, nin-nda); elsewhere the simple form (fula-o, coo-an). The Agreement page gives these forms in detail.

1979 usage

In 1979, these referents are presented as separate relative pronouns (vo, ve, van, lan…), written after the verb (Keita 1979, p. 88-89): Domaa n pendu vo sèsa “the shirt that you bought has torn”. The Bible writes the same marker attached by a hyphen at the end of the relative clause; the form vo almost never appears on its own. Follow the Bible. The description of Southern Kissi points the same way: the noun's class ending is a suffix placed at the end of the relative clause (Childs 1995, p. 285-286).

docs.title: 2. Compound words
docs.text:
The hyphen joins the elements of a compound noun whose parts keep their form (in Southern Kissi, these non-fixed compounds are pronounced as separate words (Childs 1995, p. 216)): Cɛi-Hala-o “the house of God” Gen 28:17, fuɲa-mamaa “ancestor”, fonda-loamaa-lasálàá “altar (place where sacrifices are burnt)”, cɛi-kola “tent (house of cloth)”.

Very common compounds are often written as a single word: vanapɔnɔɔ “man”, vanalanɔɔ “woman”, halataalaa “sky”. See Compound nouns.

docs.title: 3. Reduplicated words
docs.text: A word repeated to express intensity, distribution or repetition is written with a hyphen: taw-taw “very much indeed”, ɲɛ-ɲɛ “anything at all”, yɛ́-yɛ́ “each kind”, bɛndu-bɛnduan “very big (ones)”.

docs.title: The prefix n'
docs.text: The nasal prefix n' is attached by an apostrophe to the following word: n'van tɔ́ “ten people”. See Consonants.

docs.title: Summary
Kisiei–English dictionary
docs.text:
This dictionary is generated automatically from the project's lexicon (4250 entries). Words follow the Kisiei alphabetical order (ɛ after e, ŋ and ɲ after n, ɔ after o); tone marks are ignored for sorting. The underline of each word shows its source, as elsewhere in this guide: Attested in the Bible (with a reference to one occurrence), Confirmed by a speaker, Respelled from Keita 1979, To check, or Southern Kissi (Childs 2000 only, not attested in the North). To look up a word from English, see the English–Kisiei index; for words grouped by theme, see the word lists. The full lexicon is also available as CSV, TSV, LIFT and CLDF in the repository.

bùwàá v. — Southern Kissi only — hem. Childs 2000, p. 36

cɔ́lɔ̀ɔ̀-cɔ́lɔ̀ɔ̀ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — sound of heavy rain or water pouring. Childs 2000, p. 55

cɔ̀ŋgáŋcɔ̀ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — hopping, with a hopping motion. Childs 2000, p. 56

dɛnɔɔ n. (o), pl. dɛnndan — thing, matter, deed. Other forms: dɛnɛ, dɛnnda. Gen 2:9

diolan n. (lan) — name; renown. Other forms: diola. Gen 2:19

diomndo n. (o), pl. diomndan — voice, sound; word; language. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): voice, word; also advice, answer, promise; abuse. Other forms: diom, diomnda. Gen 3:8

díó n. (o), pl. díláŋ — Southern Kissi only — being in the right. Childs 2000, p. 82

dòkpòó n. (o), pl. dòkpòláŋ — Southern Kissi only — pounded rice flour; rice bread. Childs 2000, p. 86

dólàá n. (o), pl. dólàláŋ — Southern Kissi only — weaver's spool of thread. Childs 2000, p. 86

icali n. — residence; (va icali) live, dwell. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): stay, live (cited as a form of càllé 'sit'). Judg 8:17

icɔllo n. — evening, night. Gen 1:5

icɔl adv. — in the evening, at night. Gen 1:5

idiiyo adv. — in the morning, early. Other forms: idii. Gen 19:27

idii adv. — in the morning. Gen 19:2

ifalenndo n. — ephod (doma ifalenndo, priestly garment). Other forms: ifalen. Exod 28:6

ihɛllan n. — sea (mɛmma ihɛllan). Other forms: ihɛlma, ihɛl. Gen 1:10

ihini adv. — lying down. 2 Kgs 9:16

ɗííyɛ̀-ɗííyɛ̀ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — cheeping of chicks. Childs 2000, p. 79

ɗíká ideo. — Southern Kissi only — stresses an arrival. Childs 2000, p. 79

ikɛi postp. — with, beside. Gen 5:24

ikɔɔ adj. — poor, needy. Other forms: ikɔɔa. Exod 22:24

ɗìkpàá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — supervisor of initiates (women's society). Childs 2000, p. 79

ɗìkpà-céŋgòó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — third-ranking supervisor (bush school). Childs 2000, p. 79

ɗìkpà-léndòó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — second-ranking supervisor (women's society). Childs 2000, p. 79

ɗìlìŋàá v. — Southern Kissi only — pack down, compress, tamp; oppress. Childs 2000, p. 79

imamaa n. — descendants, generations. Other forms: imama. Gen 5:1

imɔnɔɔ adj. — grievous, bitter, of mourning. Other forms: imɔnɔ, imɔnɔlan, imɔnɔlen. Gen 50:11

ɗì-nàúwá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — butcher (who slaughters cattle). Childs 2000, p. 78

inɛɛ adv. — somewhere, elsewhere; (with negation) anywhere. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): somewhere, anywhere (said by older speakers). Other forms: inɛɛle. Luke 10:33

iɲíí n. — pity, mercy; (tuinun … iɲíí) have mercy on. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): sorrow, pity, mercy. Jonah 3:10

ɗìòŋgòó v. — Southern Kissi only — have an erection. Childs 2000, p. 83

ɗìòùwɔ̀ɔ́ v. — Southern Kissi only — be mushy, overcooked; be limp, unable to move (sick baby). Childs 2000, p. 83

ɗìɔ́ɔ́ n. (o), pl. dɛ̀ɛ́láŋ — Southern Kissi only — dough of pounded rice flour (with banana, sometimes honey). Childs 2000, p. 84

ipalaa n. — day(time), morning. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): afternoon. Other forms: ipala. Gen 1:5

ipala adv. — in the daytime. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): afternoon. Gen 1:5

ipulu n. — offspring; (naŋ ipúlú) be fruitful. Gen 1:22

isɛ interj. — greetings, hello. Gen 27:18

ɗìsìŋàá v. — Southern Kissi only — strike (on the head); squeeze hard; heap up. Childs 2000, p. 84

isiòòn n. — fear. Gen 15:1

isisi adv. — standing. Gen 18:2

isɔw n. — blemish, flaw. 2 Sam 14:25

itambu n. — ruin, nothingness; (cuu itambu) come to ruin. Hos 10:7

ɗìùwó v. — Southern Kissi only — be dirty. Childs 2000, p. 85

ɗíù ideo. — Southern Kissi only — stresses throwing out. Childs 2000, p. 84

ɗìyàá v. — Southern Kissi only — be mature, ripe. Childs 2000, p. 85

iyama n. — judgement, sentence. Jer 39:5

iyongban-yongbannde n. — (waters) surging, raging. Ps 46:4

i pron. — I (subject). Gen 1:29

ɗì ideo. — Southern Kissi only — sound and manner of a blow. Childs 2000, p. 76

ɗí ideo. — Southern Kissi only — stresses movement reaching its goal. Childs 2000, p. 76

docs.text:
káádɛ̂ìyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — card (comb for carding cotton). Childs 2000, p. 140

kààfàá v. — Southern Kissi only — tie loosely; grimace, bare one's teeth; suck in one's lips. Childs 2000, p. 140

kaalaa v. — love, cherish. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): love, be in love with. Keita 1979, p. 110

káálàá n. (o), pl. káálàláŋ — Southern Kissi only — drinking cup. Childs 2000, p. 140

káálen n. (len) — (foreign) land, land of exile. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): area, land, place; foreign area; also taboo, totem, clan. Lev 26:34

kaamaa n., pl. kaamaalan — awesome thing, miracle; awesome. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): amazing, incredible, wonderful. Other forms: kaamaala. Gen 28:17

káándáá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — place of sacrifice, sacrifice rock. Childs 2000, p. 141

kaandennɔɔ n. (o), pl. kaandennda — pupil, disciple. Other forms: kaandennɔ. Isa 50:4

kaandennɔ n., pl. kaandennda — disciple. Other forms: kaandeŋaa. Luke 14:27

kaanden n. (len) — worship assembly, prayer; (Keita) school, prayer. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): foreign land; school, church (GK). Exod 12:16

kaandian v. — disguise oneself. 1 Kgs 22:30

kààndìá v. — Southern Kissi only — dam (a stream); whip several times. Childs 2000, p. 142

kaangoo n. (o), pl. kaangoa — termite; moth. Keita 1979, p. 136

káángoo n. (o) — hammer. Jer 10:4

kaan n. — indigo; blue. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): indigo tree and the dark blue dye from its bark. Exod 25:4

kààŋgòó n. (o), pl. kààŋgùéí — Southern Kissi only — large forest tree with small plum-like edible fruit. Childs 2000, p. 142

kààŋgùáŋ n. (ma), pl. kààŋgòléŋ — Southern Kissi only — fruit and juice of the kààŋgòó tree. Childs 2000, p. 142

kààɲìá v. — Southern Kissi only — force open (to check), push apart branches on a path. Childs 2000, p. 142

kaasonɔɔ n. (o), pl. kaasonnda — elder; adult, grown-up ; elder, old person; (pl.) elders. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): adult, middle-aged person. Other forms: kaasonnda, kaasoŋaa. Gen 48:18

kaasoo n. (o), pl. kaasolan — prison. Gen 39:20

kaa n. — roof, ceiling. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): attic, area above the mats forming the ceiling. 1 Kgs 7:3

kàá1 n. — fox, jackal. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): small dog-like forest animal, a kind of wolf. Other forms: kàà. Judg 15:4

kàá2 v. — Southern Kissi only — clear one's throat, hawk. Childs 2000, p. 140

káà n., pl. káàlan — way of acting, conduct; fault. Other forms: kaala. Lev 18:3

kabilaa n. (o) — clan. Keita 1979, p. 142

kabi prep. — since, from (time). Matt 25:34

kácò ideo. — Southern Kissi only — violent spitting (of mucus). Childs 2000, p. 143

kádáá n. (o), pl. kádéí — Southern Kissi only — swamp vine or tree used to cure yaws. Childs 2000, p. 143

kádá ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (stuck) fast. Childs 2000, p. 143

kádì ideo. — Southern Kissi only — bone-dry (hole, hollow). Childs 2000, p. 143

kádò ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (snatch) at once; all of a sudden. Childs 2000, p. 143

kafalaa v. — fold (the hands); (kafalan) embrace, grasp. Other forms: kafala, káfàlà, kafalanndo. Prov 6:10

kafalan n. — injustice. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): cheating, deceit, trickery. Deut 24:17

kàfèìyó v. — Southern Kissi only — excuse; ask for leave or permission. Childs 2000, p. 143

kafoo n. (o), pl. kafolan — feast, festival. Other forms: kafo, kafola. Gen 29:22

káfú ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (hang on, grab) tightly. Childs 2000, p. 143

kákáá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — meanness, stinginess. Childs 2000, p. 144

kákásá-kákásá ideo. — Southern Kissi only — messily, hastily, slapdash. Childs 2000, p. 144

kákáù ideo. — Southern Kissi only — rough, bumpy. Childs 2000, p. 144

kalaa1 adj. — itself, the very (one); whole, entire. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): indeed, very, particular, itself. Other forms: kalalen, kalan, kalale. Gen 6:16

kalaa2 n. (o) — mother. Other forms: kala. Gen 27:11

kalaa3 v. — dig up, unearth. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): dig or pull out. Keita 1979, p. 110

kàlábùlùkáá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — worm-like non-poisonous burrowing snake. Childs 2000, p. 144

kàláfìɔ́ n. (o), pl. kàláfìá — Southern Kissi only — queen termite. Childs 2000, p. 145

kàlàlíó n. (o), pl. kàlàlíá — Southern Kissi only — mother-in-law (husband's mother). Childs 2000, p. 145

kàlàmàá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — small spoon-shaped calabash. Childs 2000, p. 145

kala-mamaa n. (o) — grandmother; ancestress. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): grandmother, old woman. Other forms: kala-mama. Gen 24:60

kàlàmándàá n. (o), pl. kàlàmándàŋ — Southern Kissi only — fenced garden; fenced bathing area, bath pan. Childs 2000, p. 145

kàlàmɔ́ɔ́ n. (o), pl. kàlàmɔ́ɔ́wá — Southern Kissi only — teacher of Islam, pilgrim (el Hadj). Childs 2000, p. 145

kalamulan n. — grams. Other forms: kalamula. Gen 24:22

kàlándéfù n. (o), pl. kàlándéfùá — Southern Kissi only — mother-in-law (wife's mother). Childs 2000, p. 145

kalangɛnɔɔ n. (o) — shoemaker. Keita 1979, p. 145

kalankafoo n. (o) — ghost, spirit of the dead. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): ghost of a dead person not yet among the ancestors. Other forms: kalankafo. Keita 1979, p. 150

kalaŋaa v. — be dug up, laid bare, turned up; pull out, bring up. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): (middle of 'dig up') be dug up, uprooted. Other forms: kalaŋan, kalaŋanin, kalaŋanndo. 2 Sam 22:16

kàláŋndó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — palm-fibre hamper ('kinja'); fetish worn at the neck or waist; remedy for beriberi. Childs 2000, p. 145

kaloo adj. — hard; difficult; (nila kalua) stubborn. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): hard, difficult; also sharp, strong, effective; ripe. Other forms: kalu, kalua, kalula, kalulan. Deut 21:18

kamaa n. (o) — elephant. 1 Kgs 10:18

kàmàcíŋndó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — elephant rat (long-nosed). Childs 2000, p. 146

kamafoeinɔɔ n. (o) — photographer. Keita 1979, p. 145

kamalindoŋnden n. (len) — swing. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): swing, usually made of vines. Keita 1979, p. 163

kàmásɔ̀lɔ́ŋndó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — variety of rice (said to have first grown from elephant dung). Childs 2000, p. 146

kàmàtìkèíyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — leafy vegetable like collard greens, seeds used for sauce. Childs 2000, p. 146

kambalaa n. (o) — insect. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): a large edible grasshopper. Lev 11:20

kambɛiyo n. (o), pl. kambɛilan — basket. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): large basket, hamper. Matt 14:20

kanalanndo v. — warn, admonish, rebuke; (pl. kanalannda) warnings. Other forms: kanalan, kanalannda, kanalanndan. Exod 19:21

kàndàá1 n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — dam, fish trap. Childs 2000, p. 146

kàndàá2 v. — Southern Kissi only — dam up (a stream); beat, whip, flog. Childs 2000, p. 146

kàndàkpùpùèìyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — car, automobile. Childs 2000, p. 147

kanda v. — guard, protect. Other forms: kandanin. Gen 3:24

kándéléŋ n. (le) — Southern Kissi only — braid of a woman's hair. Childs 2000, p. 147

kandolan n. — bars, crossbars. Other forms: kandola. Exod 26:26

kandoncindo n. (o) — gum (of the teeth). Keita 1979, p. 131

kandɔɔ v. — begin ; begin; beginning; (kandɔɔ …) starting from. Other forms: kandu, kandunin. Gen 1:1

kándùáŋ n. (ma), pl. kándùléŋ — Southern Kissi only — first palm oil. Childs 2000, p. 147

kándùléŋ n. (le) — Southern Kissi only — old worn dark-stained trousers of a child. Childs 2000, p. 147

kangalan adv. — surely, certainly. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): truly; marks obligation, must. Gen 41:32

kangbaa n. — sideburns. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): sideburns; also an agreement with a deceitful person, promise. Keita 1979, p. 15

kangboo n. (o), pl. kangboa — pigeon, dove. Other forms: kangbo. Gen 15:9

káníéí n. (i), pl. kánííŋ — Southern Kissi only — money. Childs 2000, p. 148

kanikokoe interj. — cry of joy, congratulations. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): (noun) congratulations. Keita 1979, p. 120

kani conj. — because, for. Gen 2:3

kankpoo n. (o) — wood pigeon. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): dove, pigeon. Keita 1979, p. 136

kan det. — those (persons). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): these (a class), labelled proximal. Gen 6:4

káŋgàá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — bamboo or raffia mat (for ceilings and drying produce). Childs 2000, p. 148

kàŋgàlàá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — deceit, cheating, greed. Childs 2000, p. 148

káŋgáláŋndó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — obligation, duty. Childs 2000, p. 148

kàŋgbòkpòó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — gourd with ashes inside used in spinning cotton. Childs 2000, p. 148

káŋgóó n. (o), pl. káŋgóláŋ — Southern Kissi only — deep-set, sunken eyes. Childs 2000, p. 149

kàŋnda n. — paths, ways; tracks, footsteps. Other forms: kàŋ, kàŋndan. Ps 25:4

kàɲàá v. — Southern Kissi only — force open (mouth, door), check by opening (ear of corn); (kàɲàá hɔ̀ltéŋ) tease. Childs 2000, p. 149

kaolaa v. — love. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): love, be in love with. Other forms: kaola. Gen 22:2

kásáá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — small reddish swamp mouse (edible). Childs 2000, p. 149

kasa v. — refuse, resist. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): resist. Prov 1:24

kasio n. (o) — offence, fault; (del kasi) offend, sin against. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): rules of a (secret) society; the offence of breaking them. Other forms: kasi, kasila. Gen 40:1

kátáá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — chief's enclosure, inner compound. Childs 2000, p. 150

kàùwé1 n. (i) — Southern Kissi only — (tobacco) pipe. Childs 2000, p. 150

kàùwé2 n. (i) — Southern Kissi only — potion keeping evil spirits from a house or thieves from rice. Childs 2000, p. 150

kau ideo. — (take, snatch away) all at once. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): suddenness of taking, as an eagle snatching; used with 'take'. Isa 57:13

kàváá n. (o) — bright spot (on the skin). Other forms: kava. Lev 13:19

kawve n. (i) — bean. Keita 1979, p. 139

kayaa n. (o), pl. kayalan — basket. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): fish basket. Keita 1979, p. 159

kayakayaa v. — surround, entangle; interlace. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): (ropes, vines) be tangled or twisted together; be overgrown. Other forms: kayakaya, kayakayan.

kàyěŋndé n. (i), pl. kàyěŋndóŋ — Southern Kissi only — sword grass (vine?) with very sharp edges, hard to uproot. Childs 2000, p. 150

kâyìàŋ-kâyìàŋ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — lurching, wobbling (like a drunk). Childs 2000, p. 151

ka part. — (after a reduplicated indefinite) whatever, of every kind.

ká adv. — Southern Kissi only — for a long time, far, a lot. Childs 2000, p. 139

kèbínɔ̀ɔ́ n. (o), pl. kèbíá — Southern Kissi only — smith, metal worker, goldsmith (older name). Childs 2000, p. 158

kèédei n. (i) — threshold. Gen 19:6

kééfáyɔ́lɔ̀ɔ́ n. (o), pl. kééfáyɔ́lúéí — Southern Kissi only — tree species (female in swamps, male on dry ground) with oil-bearing fruit and white latex. Childs 2000, p. 151

keeku v. — lead through, make pass through. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): pass through or by; experience; repeat. Other forms: keekan. Ps 106:9

keelaa v. — go about, walk about; (keela kɔllo) meditate, reflect. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): stroll, saunter, walk about. Other forms: keela. Ps 1:2

keeliaa v. — lead about; look around. Gen 13:10

kèèlúŋndó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — a small species of bird. Childs 2000, p. 152

kééndéíyé n. (i) — Southern Kissi only — traditional razor blade. Childs 2000, p. 158

keenduu v. — pick off, strip off (fruit, leaves); (keendun) fall out (hair). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): pick (many fruits), plural of 'pick, pluck'; (middle) drop, fall. Other forms: keendun. Dan 4:11

kèéŋndó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — ground squirrel. Childs 2000, p. 158

keesoo n. (o) — (fine) linen. Other forms: keese, keesela. Exod 39:27

kééwéé-kééwéé ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (cut) into very small pieces. Childs 2000, p. 153

kefii n. (i), pl. kefon — sting, stinger (of an insect); (kefun) chaff. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): rice chaff, husks; stinger of an insect. Other forms: kefun. 1 Cor 15:55

keilan n. — passing, way one walks, path. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): passing; way, track (plural of 'pass by'). Prov 4:26

keiyo v. — pass through, cross; tread on. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): pass by or through; undergo. Other forms: kei, keinin. Gen 12:6

kèìyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — gate. Childs 2000, p. 153

kékélé ideo. — (dry) completely. Gen 41:6

kèké n. (o), pl. kèkíá — Southern Kissi only — father, paternal uncle; address term for a male superior. Childs 2000, p. 159

kelaa v. — walk ; walk; behave, live. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): walk around (e.g. to sell). Other forms: kela, kelanin. Gen 1:20

kèlàá v. — Southern Kissi only — cut, trim (grass, hair), shave. Childs 2000, p. 159

kélàá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — small grey fish. Childs 2000, p. 153

kelanndo v. — walk about, wander. Other forms: kelan. Gen 4:12

kelekeloo n. (o) — whooping cough. Keita 1979, p. 161

kélélé ideo. — (bitter) intensely. Rev 8:11

keleŋaa v. — hurry, be quick. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): hurry, make haste. Other forms: keleŋa, keleŋanin. Exod 2:18

keleŋa adv. — quickly. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): (verb) hurry, do at once. Gen 19:22

kèlèŋgàà adv. — Southern Kissi only — perhaps, maybe, probably. Childs 2000, p. 160

keleŋnde n. (i) — slit drum, wooden xylophone drum. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): wooden drum: a hollow log with holes, beaten with sticks. Keita 1979, p. 163

kéléŋndó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — glans (of the penis). Childs 2000, p. 154

kéléŋ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — straight ahead; (Liberia) a term of abuse. Childs 2000, p. 154

kelɛi bai n. — bracelet. Keita 1979, p. 144

kelɛi n'sianiei n. — gold ring. Keita 1979, p. 144

kelɛi pelei n. — anklet. Keita 1979, p. 144

kelɛi suei n. — finger ring. Keita 1979, p. 144

kelɛi n. (i), pl. kelan — ring, bracelet. Gen 24:22

kélíɛ́ɛ́-kélíɛ́ɛ́ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (scratch) briskly but lightly. Childs 2000, p. 160

kěllò n. (o), pl. kěltáŋ — Southern Kissi only — crust, scab; dried nasal mucus. Childs 2000, p. 160

kémsáá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — palm kernel shell. Childs 2000, p. 155

kèndìó n. (o), pl. kèndìláŋ — Southern Kissi only — rattling, mucus-filled cough. Childs 2000, p. 155

kendu adj. — difficult, hard. Gen 18:14

kengela v. — dry up, harden; stiffen, wither (hand); (kengelɛi) dry, dried out. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): be dry; cook until dry; be thin; be so cold as to shiver, have a fit. Other forms: kengelan, kengelɛi, kengelɛila. Deut 28:23

kennun v. — be given. John 19:11

ken det. — that (i class). Gen 2:22

kéŋgélɛ́ŋɛ́ŋ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — sound of a light or thin person falling. Childs 2000, p. 161

kèŋgèmùkíó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — rice flour with tiny hard grains (made from dɛ̀mdɛ̀mndó). Childs 2000, p. 156

kéŋgóó n. (o), pl. kéŋgéláŋ — Southern Kissi only — fault, defect, flaw. Childs 2000, p. 161

kèŋndóŋ n. (ŋ) — Southern Kissi only — xylophone. Childs 2000, p. 157

kèŋndó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — leprosy (with twisted, decaying fingers). Childs 2000, p. 156

keo v. — give, offer. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): give, offer. Other forms: ke, kenin. Gen 49:10

kesu n. — chest, box; ark (kesu kpemaa). Gen 50:26

kèwèí n. (i), pl. kèwɔ̌ŋ — Southern Kissi only — tree with small fragrant flowers (dry season), used to scent oil. Childs 2000, p. 157

kèwèkèwèí n. (i), pl. kèwèkèwɔ̌ŋ — Southern Kissi only — tall fruitless valley palm resembling a coconut tree. Childs 2000, p. 157

kèwɛ́lɔ̀ɔ́ n. (o), pl. kèwɛ́ltáŋ — Southern Kissi only — clever or amusing way of doing something (weaving, dancing). Childs 2000, p. 162

kéyěŋ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (fall down) softly. Childs 2000, p. 157

ke v. — give; (ke diolan) name. Other forms: keo, kenin. Gen 1:5

kê ideo. — Southern Kissi only — all the way, a long time or distance, on and on. Childs 2000, p. 157

kɛɛlen n. (len), pl. kɛɛyan — raffia rib, pole (used as a beam). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): raffia, palm fronds (esp. of the piassava palm), swamp bamboo. Keita 1979, p. 28

kɛɛmiaa v. — adorn, decorate; overlay (with gold, silver). Prov 25:11

kɛɛmianɔɔ n. (o) — decorator. Keita 1979, p. 145

kɛɛsiaa v. — decide, resolve, plan. Isa 14:27

kɛɛyaa v. — trim, cut, reduce. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): cut (nails), operate on; clean the tapping hole of a palm-wine tree. Keita 1979, p. 110

kɛɛ v. — refuse, reject. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): refuse, disagree with, deny (middle form). Other forms: kɛɛnin. Gen 4:5

kɛi n. — thread, yarn. Other forms: kɛila. Gen 14:23

kɛkɛwvo n. (o), pl. kɛkɛwlan — scale (of a fish). Keita 1979, p. 136

kɛkɛ det. — any, whatever; (o kɛkɛ) anything, whatever. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): any (takes the noun-class prefix of its referent). Keita 1979, p. 71

kɛlɛmasaa n. (o) — war chief. Keita 1979, p. 156

kɛmbɛi kokoei n. — coconut. Keita 1979, p. 139

kɛmbɛi kɔi n. — spine. Keita 1979, p. 131

kɛmbɛi laboloei n. — Adam's apple. Keita 1979, p. 131

kɛmbɛi n. (i) — palm kernel. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): palm kernel, coconut; wedge; vulgar term for the female genitals. Keita 1979, p. 139

kɛmɛ num. — hundred. Gen 5:3

kɛmikɛmiaa v. — engrave, carve (ornaments). 1 Kgs 7:36

kɛmndan n. (an) — dew. Gen 27:28

kɛndia n. — health, well-being; peace, safety; (muungu kɛndia) come back safe and sound. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): health, general well-being, being at peace with the ancestors. Gen 28:21

kɛndɔɔ adj. — good; beautiful. Other forms: kɛndɛ, kɛndɛa, kɛndɛi, kɛndɛla, kɛndɛlan, kɛndɛan, kɛndɛlen, kɛndɛn, kɛndɔn. Gen 2:9

la pron. — you (pl., subject); lan-class pronoun. Gen 1:11

lebɛngu adv. — underneath, below. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): under, between. Josh 7:22

lecoo adv. — on top, above. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): also 'about, concerning'. Gen 1:2

lediom n. — truth, faithfulness, uprightness. Ps 40:11

leeloo postp. — on the other side of, beyond. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): across, on the other side; in Liberia also a name for Guinea. Judg 10:9

leemu-leemu ideo. — supple, pliant, bending. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): flexibly. Other forms: leemu-leemoo. Gen 49:24

leendo n. (o), pl. leenda — agama lizard. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): gecko, a black lizard. Keita 1979, p. 136

lèéŋndé n. (i) — Southern Kissi only — waste. Childs 2000, p. 226

lee n., pl. leelan — horn; (horn) trumpet. Other forms: leela. Dan 7:8

lefoo n. — father-in-law; (lefu … laandoo) mother-in-law. Other forms: lefu. Exod 3:1

lefuo n. (o), pl. lefua — in-law: son-in-law, daughter-in-law, father-in-law, mother-in-law. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): in-law. Other forms: lefu. Keita 1979, p. 134

le hee conj. — then; therefore.

lèíyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — kind of flying insect (stings). Childs 2000, p. 229

lekaando adj. — of worship, cultic. Other forms: lekaan, lekaannda, lekaandan, lekaandon. Deut 16:8

lekáá n. — absence, exile (o lekáá 'away, banished, lost').

lekɛ́ndɛi adv. — truly, really. 1 Kgs 17:24

lekɔɔli adv. — outside, on the outside. Gen 6:14

lekɔɔ postp. — on (the body), on oneself; next to. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): on, near, next to, behind. Gen 27:11

lèkpààdóó n. — Southern Kissi only — Tuesday (market day). Childs 2000, p. 226

lelan conj. — therefore, so. Gen 2:24

lemasaa n., pl. lemasalan — kingship, majesty; (after a noun) royal. Other forms: lemasa, lemasala. Job 40:10

lemboo adj., pl. lemboa — virgin (unmarried girl). Other forms: lembu. Gen 24:16

lembulten n. (len) — lemon, lime. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): citrus fruit: orange, lemon, lime. Keita 1979, p. 139

lémcíóó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — kind of bird (quick). Childs 2000, p. 226

lenamta n. — blemish, defect (nɔ lenamta loo 'without blemish'). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): a crippled or handicapped person. Exod 12:5

lende adv. — thus, so, in this way, like that. Gen 1:7

lèndè- adj. — Southern Kissi only — young, small; second, deputy (vice-). Childs 2000, p. 227

lendulun v. — sell oneself, pawn oneself (as a servant). Other forms: lendulɔn. Lev 25:39

lenin adv. — inside, within; in (after the noun). Gen 6:14

len det. — this, that (len class). Gen 2:3

lèŋèlàá v. — Southern Kissi only — reduce, slim down (by trimming or tying). Childs 2000, p. 227

léŋé-léŋé ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (slim down) even more, very thin. Childs 2000, p. 227

lèŋndó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — louse-like insect; worm found in refuse. Childs 2000, p. 230

leo n. (o), pl. leelan — horn. Dan 8:3

lepalaa adv. — daily, every day (lepalaa-lepala). Other forms: lepala. Luke 9:23

lepɛŋndo n. — ignorance; (o sina lepɛŋndo nin) unknowingly. Other forms: lepɛŋ, lepɛŋnde. Lev 4:2

lepɔtɔllo adj. — forced, hard (labour). Other forms: lepɔtɔltan, lepɔtɔl, lepɔtɔlta. 1 Kgs 4:6

lèsɔ́ɔ́ n. (o), pl. lèsúá — Southern Kissi only — cry-baby. Childs 2000, p. 230

le tùú conj. — because.

léùléù adj. — Southern Kissi only — flexible, pliant. Childs 2000, p. 230

lèùŋndó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — family (archaic). Childs 2000, p. 230

lèùwè n. (i) — Southern Kissi only — kind of tree (slow to dry). Childs 2000, p. 228

levil adv. — far, far away; (lɔ́ɔ́ levil) long ago. Matt 15:8

levundu n. — shadow; (o levundu nin) in riddles. Ps 109:23

lèwɔ́ɔ́ n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — palm butter (palm-nut sauce). Childs 2000, p. 230

leyáá num. — three times; (kɛmɛ leyáá) three hundred. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): three times. Other forms: leyàá. Gen 5:22

leyinndo n. — flame, blazing fire; furnace. Other forms: leyin, leyinndan. Exod 9:8

le1 part. — not (clause-final negation). Other forms: te. Gen 1:2

le2 prep. — for, because of. Gen 1:2

lɛan n. (an) — honey. 1 Sam 14:25

lɛɛfɛnndo n. (o), pl. lɛɛfɛnnda — swallow (bird). Ps 84:4

lɛɛlɛ n. — hour. Luke 23:44

lɛɛndei n. (i), pl. lɛɛndun — twig, bough. Matt 24:32

lɛɛndo n. (o) — machete, cutlass. Isa 10:34

lɛɛnduu v. — hang up, attach, fasten (several things); hang (several people). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): hang many things (plural of làndɔ̀ɔ́). Exod 25:12

lɛ́ɛ́ŋ-ìcɔ̀cɔ̀ɔ́ n. (o), pl. lɛ́ɛ́ŋndá-ìcɔ̀cɔ̀láŋ — Southern Kissi only — small, slightly curved cutlass. Childs 2000, p. 228

lɛ̀ɛ́ŋndó v. — Southern Kissi only — be over-anxious, tremble (as when beaten). Childs 2000, p. 228

lɛ́ɛ́siɛn ideo. — lying lifeless. 1 Sam 17:52

lɛ́ɛ́ù-lɛ̀ɛ̀ù ideo. — Southern Kissi only — bending easily. Childs 2000, p. 228

lɛ́ɛ́yáŋ n. (ma) — Southern Kissi only — bush beans. Childs 2000, p. 228

lɛfɔɔ n. (o) — flag, banner. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): flag; also a wind-blown bamboo noisemaker that scares birds. Other forms: lɛfɛ. Keita 1979, p. 159

lɛ̀ìyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — kind of red ant (painful bite). Childs 2000, p. 229

lɛ́kpɛ́í n. (i) — Southern Kissi only — sobbing, crying a lot. Childs 2000, p. 229

lɛlɔn n. — leprosy. Keita 1979, p. 161

lɛ̀mbɛ̀-làkpáùwó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — girl's waist cloth. Childs 2000, p. 229

lɛmbɛla n. — breeches, undergarments (lɛmbɛla lebɛngulan, undertrousers). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): trousers, pants; lɛ̀mbɛ̀lɛ̀-bɛ̀ŋóó underwear. Exod 28:42

lɛmbɛvilɛiyo n. (o) — trousers. Keita 1979, p. 144

lɛ̀ŋgbɛ́sɔ́ɔ́ n. (o), pl. lɛ̀ŋgbɛ́súéí — Southern Kissi only — tree whose berry juice treats toothache. Other forms: lɛ̀ŋgbɛ́síɔ́. Childs 2000, p. 229

lɛ́ŋgbɔ̀ŋ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — flexibly, pliantly. Childs 2000, p. 229

lɛ́ŋgbùŋ- adj. — Southern Kissi only — soft, flexible, pliable. Childs 2000, p. 229

lɛŋnden n. (len), pl. lɛŋii — country, nation; land, earth. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): land, ground, area; country of origin; world, earth; floor. Other forms: lɛŋnde. Gen 1:1

lɛŋ adv. — on the ground, down. Gen 2:7

lɛu n. (o), pl. lɛa — bee. Keita 1979, p. 136

lɛvɛnndo n. — leaven, yeast. Other forms: lɛvɛn. Lev 2:11

lɛwve n. (i), pl. lɛwvon — branch. Other forms: lɛvii, lɛvun, lɛvi. Gen 49:11

lɛ adv. — still; (with negation) no longer, any more. Gen 8:12

liilaa v. — accompany, go with; lead. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): accompany, escort; (Liberian Kissi) carry halfway. Other forms: liila. Gen 14:24

líílìyé n. (i) — Southern Kissi only — charcoal marks drawn on the body. Childs 2000, p. 230

liimiaa v. — deceive. Keita 1979, p. 110

lìlìléŋ n. (le) — Southern Kissi only — material (fibre waste) used for making bags; traditional medicine. Childs 2000, p. 230

lìmbàá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — bat. Childs 2000, p. 231

lìmbàwóó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — kola nut with a sweet outer cover. Childs 2000, p. 231

límsàá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — kind of hard black-shelled insect (rice pest). Childs 2000, p. 230

linda v. — knead. Gen 18:6

lìŋndó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — rice bird (small bird that eats rice). Childs 2000, p. 231

lisaa v. — praise, glorify. Other forms: lisa, lisan, lisanin. Exod 15:1

litilio n., pl. litililan — litre (measure). Exod 16:16

liva v. — be wet, be drenched. Other forms: liviaa. Judg 6:39

loamaa v. — burn; (sálà loamaa) burnt offering. Other forms: loam, loamnin. Gen 8:20

loei n. (i), pl. loeon — star. Num 24:17

lolɛiyo adj. — bitter. Other forms: lolɛima, lolɛiyan, lolɛilen. Num 5:18

lòlló n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — kind of tree (weak roots). Childs 2000, p. 232

loloo adj. — bitter; bitterness. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): be bitter; also report someone. Exod 12:8

lólòó n. (o), pl. lólòla — gall, bile; venom. Other forms: lólò. Job 16:13

lómbòléŋ n. (le), pl. lómbùéí — Southern Kissi only — penis. Other forms: lóómbòléŋ. Childs 2000, p. 232

lòmkɔ́ɔ́ n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — kind of tree (striped). Childs 2000, p. 232

lómlómndáŋ n. (ma) — Southern Kissi only — fern. Childs 2000, p. 232

lomnden n. (len) — tail. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): tail; slang for penis. Keita 1979, p. 136

lomnɔnndo v. — burn oneself, be burnt; (noun) a burn. Other forms: lomnun, lomnɔn. Lev 13:25

lomɔɔ v. — burn. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): burn, be burning. Other forms: lom, loam, lum, loamnin, lumnin. Gen 19:28

lòmsóó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — worm found in beds often urinated on. Childs 2000, p. 232

lòndòó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — kind of savanna grass (medicinal). Childs 2000, p. 232

lon adv. — there. Gen 2:10

lóŋgbáléŋ n. (le) — Southern Kissi only — roasting spit. Childs 2000, p. 232

lóŋíó n. (o), pl. lóŋíláŋ — Southern Kissi only — small three-legged cooking pot. Other forms: lóŋíóó, lóŋgímèíyó. Childs 2000, p. 232

lòŋùèí n. (i), pl. lòŋǒŋ — Southern Kissi only — hip. Childs 2000, p. 233

looku v. — manage, contrive (how). Gen 27:20

loolio n. (o) — mud. 1 Sam 4:12

lòòlòò v. — Southern Kissi only — rape. Other forms: lóólúúwó. Childs 2000, p. 233

loonanndo adj. — commemorative; memorial. Other forms: loonan, loonannde, loonannden. Exod 13:9

loonɔnndo v. — remember. Other forms: loonun, loonunnin. Gen 8:1

loovo n. — possession, inheritance. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): legacy, inheritance. Ezek 11:15

loo postp. — without, lacking. Mark 4:25

lòsùèí n. (i), pl. lòsǒŋ — Southern Kissi only — sty; dried mucus in the eye. Childs 2000, p. 233

lou v. — remain, stay; keep on, persist. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): remain, keep on; also get lost, disappear; adopt into the family. Other forms: lonin. Exod 2:21

lovɛi n. (i) — strangulated hernia. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): hernia. Keita 1979, p. 161

lo postp. — at (someone's place) (o … lo). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): also 'to (someone)'. Gen 1:9

lɔaa v. — strike, beat; play (an instrument) ; strike, beat; play (an instrument); knock. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): hit, beat, strike. Other forms: lɔanin, lɔa. Gen 4:21

lɔalaa v. — accuse, denounce, slander. Other forms: lɔalu, lɔalunin. Dan 3:8

lɔan n. (an) — sleep. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): sleep (verb). Other forms: lɔma. Gen 2:21

lɔ̀cɔ̀ɔ́ n. (o), pl. lɔ̀cɔ̀léŋ — Southern Kissi only — slimy edible plant (also used to grease brick moulds). Childs 2000, p. 233

lɔ́-kùɛ̀ɛ́nɛ́ adv. — Southern Kissi only — when? (literally 'which market day'). Childs 2000, p. 234

lɔlnun v. — lie down to sleep, sleep; spend the night. Other forms: lɔlnin. Ps 4:9

lɔloo n. (o), pl. lɔlulan — thigh. Other forms: lɔlu. Gen 32:32

lɔlɔɔ v. — denounce, inform against, accuse. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): envy, resent; grumble against someone. 1 Sam 22:22

lɔluan n. (an) — saliva, spittle. Deut 25:9

lɔ́lúí-cìɔ́ɔ́ n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — share of meat (thigh) given to the farm owner after group hoeing. Childs 2000, p. 234

lɔ̀lùkómsáá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — kind of tree. Childs 2000, p. 234

lɔlu n. — thigh. Gen 47:29

lɔl v. — spend the night, lodge, dwell. 1 Kgs 19:9

lɔ́mbíó n. (o), pl. lɔ́mbíléŋ — Southern Kissi only — green moss (of shady places in the rainy season). Other forms: lɔ́mbíóó. Childs 2000, p. 234

lɔ̀ndìmèíyé n. (i) — Southern Kissi only — nail (metal). Childs 2000, p. 235

lɔ́ndɔ̀ŋndó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — (long) trousers. Other forms: lɔ̀mbɔ̀ɔ́. Childs 2000, p. 235

lɔngɔlian v. — roll, wallow; be defiled. Other forms: lɔngɔlianndo. Ezek 16:6

lɔ́ngùlɔn ideo. — limp, powerless; (sleep) deep. Gen 15:12

lɔ̀ŋɔ̀ɔ́ n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — kind of animal (with fine hands). Childs 2000, p. 235

lɔ̀ɔ̀-cíéíyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — kind of snake (dangerous). Childs 2000, p. 235

lɔɔmei n. (i) — nasal mucus. Keita 1979, p. 132

lɔɔnɔnndo v. — beat oneself. Isa 51:22

lɔ̀ɔ́ n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — handle; stem. Childs 2000, p. 235

lɔ́ɔ́ n. (o), pl. lɔ́ɔ́lan — week ; market; week. Deut 16:9

lɔ̀ùwɔ̀ɔ́ v. — Southern Kissi only — be cooked, be ready to eat. Childs 2000, p. 235

lɔu v. — braid, weave, spin; mould (bricks). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): plait, braid (baskets, slings). Other forms: lɔa. Exod 1:14

lɔwviaa v. — bite. Num 21:6

luakolanɔɔ n. (o) — weaver. Keita 1979, p. 145

lùáŋndé-sòòlùùwó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — ceremony to appease the ancestors (meal cooked on a rocky hill, a share left for them). Childs 2000, p. 236

lùàŋndé n. (i) — Southern Kissi only — hill, mountain; clearing on a hill; sacred place. Other forms: ráŋndé. Childs 2000, p. 235

luaŋ n. — top, upper side; north (a ba luaŋ-ndo, northward). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): upper part, up(hill). Gen 13:14

lueinun v. — go in to (a woman); (… yoomuan) take courage, be strong. Deut 31:6

lueiyo v. — bring in, put in; cause (grief). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): put in; also carry back, put away, return. Other forms: luei, lueinin. Gen 19:10

lùèíyó v. — Southern Kissi only — be sharp. Childs 2000, p. 236

luɛyaa n., pl. luɛyaalan — entrance, gate. Other forms: luɛyaala. 2 Kgs 10:8

luɛyɔɔninndo n. (o) — bribe. Deut 27:25

luɛyɔɔ v. — enter, go in; come, arrive. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): enter, come in; put in; produce in quantity (crops). Other forms: luɛi, luɛinin. Gen 6:18

lullo v. — leak; drain away. Other forms: lul. Eccl 10:18

lùmbìáŋ n. (ma), pl. lùmbèléŋ — Southern Kissi only — (piassava) palm wine. Childs 2000, p. 236

lùmbɔ́ɔ́ n. (o), pl. lùmbíáŋ — Southern Kissi only — piassava (raffia) palm, tapped for wine. Childs 2000, p. 236

lùmndé n. (i) — Southern Kissi only — deepest part of a river, whirlpool; death. Childs 2000, p. 236

lumndo n. — youngest child, last-born. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): last child born to a woman. Gen 42:13

lum v. — bake, prepare (a meal). Gen 19:3

lúŋndéŋ n. (le) — Southern Kissi only — tall dead palm tree without fronds (often struck by lightning). Childs 2000, p. 237

luŋ n. — public square; (o luŋ) in public, outside. Matt 11:16

lusullo v. — be heavy; weight. Other forms: lusul, lusulaa. 1 Sam 17:5

luusian v. — wander, go astray; be lost. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): play tricks, act foolishly; get lost, go missing. Gen 21:14

docs.text:
máàcàcà ideo. — Southern Kissi only — sticky. Childs 2000, p. 238

màákèétìyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — vaccination. Childs 2000, p. 238

mààla n. — abomination, disgraceful act, breach of a taboo (tosa mààla, commit an outrage). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): taboo, behavioural restriction (e.g. incest), whose breach brings illness; obligation, debt. Other forms: mààlan. Lev 18:22

maalianndo v. — help one another. Other forms: maalian. Isa 41:6

maalon n. — rice; wheat. Gen 30:14

mààmàdúnɔ́ n. (o), pl. mààmàdúá — Southern Kissi only — member of the lineage for whom eating baboon is taboo. Childs 2000, p. 239

máámúúléŋ n. (le) — Southern Kissi only — hide-and-seek (game). Childs 2000, p. 239

máándo n. (o) — shrine, place of worship. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): place of worship; secret meeting place of the men in the forest. Other forms: máánnda, máánndan. Judg 17:5

máànùú interj. — Southern Kissi only — sorry! (sympathy, condolence). Other forms: máánùú. Childs 2000, p. 239

màásàlèìyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — large storage sack (about 100 kg, for coffee). Childs 2000, p. 239

mààsííyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — machine; computer. Other forms: màsííyó. Childs 2000, p. 239

mààwɛ̀ɛ̀ part. — Southern Kissi only — what kind of, like what. Childs 2000, p. 239

mààyòó n. (o), pl. mààyèláŋ — Southern Kissi only — fish poison; (slang) sex. Childs 2000, p. 239

maa conj. — that (complementizer). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): also 'as'. Gen 1:4

màá n. (o), pl. màáláŋ — Southern Kissi only — group organized for joint labour, cooperative. Childs 2000, p. 238

macali adv. — backwards, onto one's back. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): lying on one's back. 1 Sam 4:18

macɛlu adv. — far, far away. Isa 57:19

màcùàà adv. — Southern Kissi only — really, the most; thus, like that. Other forms: màcùà. Childs 2000, p. 239

màdàlííléŋ n. (le) — Southern Kissi only — tangerine. Childs 2000, p. 239

makoo n. (o) — need; matter, affair. Luke 5:31

makɔɔ adv. — behind, backwards, at the back. Gen 9:23

malaa v. — help. Other forms: mala, malanin. Gen 2:18

málàá n. (o), pl. málàá — Southern Kissi only — fish bait (small worms). Other forms: mâllá. Childs 2000, p. 240

malalɛi n. (i) — pancreas (Keita). Keita 1979, p. 132

malan conj. — before; and only then, then. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): before, earlier; soon. Gen 5:5

máláŋndó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — glue. Childs 2000, p. 240

màlìkpáléí n. (i) — Southern Kissi only — unthreshed rice. Childs 2000, p. 240

malnun v. — give up, let go of; remit (a debt); (malnun kɔl) breathe one's last. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): drop, leave or lose (by itself). Other forms: malnɔnndo, malnunnin, malnɔn. Gen 49:33

maloo n. (o) — hippopotamus. Keita 1979, p. 136

malɔɔ v. — leave, let go, release; put, place; forgive (malɔɔ … haki); (noun) forgiveness. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): leave, depart; drop; forgive. Other forms: mal. Exod 3:19

maluaŋ n. — north. Exod 26:20

mamaa n. — grandparent, ancestor; grandchild. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): grandmother, old woman. Other forms: mama. 1 Kgs 15:11

mamanndo v. — mock. Keita 1979, p. 114

mamɔɔ v. — laugh. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): laugh, joke. Other forms: mam, mem, mamnin. Judg 16:25

mànàwɛ́íyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — variety of banana (tasty). Childs 2000, p. 241

mandaa v. — keep, guard, look after. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): take care of, raise (animals); mind. Other forms: manda, mandanin. Gen 2:15

mandanndo v. — keep oneself (from), beware; store up. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): take care of oneself. Other forms: mandan. Luke 12:15

mandenɔɔ n. (o), pl. mandea — diviner, charmer. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): diviner, fortune teller, medicine man; also a Muslim. Deut 18:11

mandrakɔr n. — mandrake. Gen 30:14

mangalaa v. — change; (mangalan) be changed, be different. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): change (clothes, behaviour); play magic, transform by magic. Other forms: mangala, mangalan, mangalanin, mangalɛi. Acts 17:30

mangaliaa v. — falsify, rig; (mangaliala) sorceries, magic tricks. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): change many things; play magic. Other forms: mangaliala. Amos 8:5

manne n. — manna. Exod 16:31

man det. — this, that (an class). Gen 1:2

màŋcáŋ n. (ŋ) — Southern Kissi only — cooked rice without sauce. Childs 2000, p. 242

máŋgáá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — dark traditional glue made from tree sap. Other forms: máŋáá. Childs 2000, p. 242

màɲjàá n. (o), pl. màɲjàláŋ — Southern Kissi only — rice swamp, especially the chief's. Childs 2000, p. 242

masaa n. (o) — king, chief. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): chief. Gen 12:15

másáá n. (o), pl. másáléŋ — Southern Kissi only — yaws (skin infection, especially of the feet). Childs 2000, p. 243

masa-ibungaa n. — governor, proconsul. Other forms: masa-ibunga. Luke 2:2

masalen n. (len) — kingdom, reign, kingship. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): chieftaincy, rule. Other forms: masale. Matt 13:52

másáŋ-kàŋgóó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — disease that pits the soles of the feet. Childs 2000, p. 243

masɛi n. — kingdom, nation. Ezek 35:10

masindɛ adj. — ancient, of old; (kabi masindɛ) from of old; (Bɛndu Yuu Masindɛ-Sindɔɔ) the Ancient of Days. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): (adj.) of an earlier time; sìndɔ̀ɔ́ 'old days'. Other forms: masindɛa, masindɛlan, masindɛla, masindɛi, masindɔɔ, masindɔn, masindɛ-sindɔɔ, masindɛ-sindɔn. Ps 78:2

mayoomoo adj. — strong, mighty; fortified; (mayoomu) strength. Other forms: mayoomu, mayoomua, mayoomulan. Ps 46:12

mâ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (reduce) to smallness. Childs 2000, p. 237

mbaa interj. — yes? (answer to a call). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): response to a greeting. Gen 27:18

mbìlíìyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — large drum (kettle drum, bass drum). Other forms: mbìlííyó. Childs 2000, p. 256

mbokponi n. — young lady. Keita 1979, p. 134

mboomaa n. (o) — hammock; litter, palanquin. Other forms: mbòòma. Keita 1979, p. 159

mbooyaa n. — pottage, stew, broth. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): thin watery sauce served over rice, residue left after making palm oil. Other forms: mbooya. 2 Kgs 4:38

mbòòyàbèí n. (i) — Southern Kissi only — guava tree. Childs 2000, p. 256

mbɔ̀ interj. — ah! alas! (exclamation). Jer 10:19

médèíyé n. (i) — Southern Kissi only — badge, medal. Other forms: méédèíyé. Childs 2000, p. 244

meilul v. — be quiet (and listen), stop talking; let off, leave (unpunished). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): stop, desist (usually from talking) for someone. Other forms: meilu. Job 13:13

meiyo1 n. — silence, quiet (o meiyo nin). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): (verb) keep quiet; set a time. Lam 3:26

meiyo2 v. — be silent. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): keep quiet. Other forms: mei, meinin. 2 Kgs 7:9

méléká ideo. — Southern Kissi only — in an unseemly or unruly way, frisky; promiscuous. Childs 2000, p. 243

mello v. — let go, allow; keep for (Keita). Other forms: mel, melnin. Exod 4:23

mèlló n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — food kept aside for someone. Childs 2000, p. 243

méŋèlěŋ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (collapse, break up) completely. Childs 2000, p. 244

mɛ̀ɛ̀kììyó n. (i) — Southern Kissi only — (beauty) scars, mostly on women. Childs 2000, p. 244

mɛɛlaa adj. — last, final. Other forms: mɛɛlaala, mɛɛlaalan, mɛɛlaalen. Neh 8:18

mɛɛlen n. (len) — breast. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): breast, breast milk; pus. Gen 21:8

mɛ́ɛ́lìíyé n. (i) — Southern Kissi only — sugar-cane press. Childs 2000, p. 245

mɛɛloo v. — end, finish, come to an end. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): also stop, reach an end or boundary. Other forms: mɛɛlu, mɛɛlunin. Gen 44:12

mɛɛlulan n. — end, last part; (o mɛɛlulan) finally, afterwards. Other forms: mɛɛlula. Dan 8:19

mɛ̀ɛ̀mɛ́í n. (i) — Southern Kissi only — sprouting palm nut. Childs 2000, p. 245

mɛɛnaa v. — curse. Keita 1979, p. 110

mɛɛndanndo v. — look, watch, observe, inspect. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): look into deeply, ponder, scrutinize. Other forms: mɛɛndan, mɛɛndannin. Gen 15:5

mɛɛndianndo v. — look around, examine, observe. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): plural of mèèndăŋndɔ́ 'look into': look around, ponder, scrutinize. Other forms: mɛɛndian. Gen 13:14

mɛɛniaa v. — curse; curse repeatedly (Keita). Other forms: mɛɛnian. 1 Kgs 2:8

mɛ́ɛ́ú ideo. — Southern Kissi only — sound of eating or swallowing (all at once). Childs 2000, p. 245

mɛɛyaa v. — sink, go under (water). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): imbibe, drink deeply; sink, dive; get oneself into trouble. Other forms: mɛɛyanin. Luke 5:7

mɛɛyan n. (an) — (breast) milk; breasts. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): breast, breast milk; also pus. Heb 5:12

mɛɛ conj. — when; as, like. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): also 'since, after, while; except, unless'. Gen 1

mɛiyo v. — leave, leave over; (mɛiyo yoomu) let live. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): leave; stop, cease (especially talking); arrange, agree. Other forms: mɛi, mɛinin. Exod 1:18

mɛ́kpɛ́nɔ́ɔ́ n. (o), pl. mɛ́kpíá — Southern Kissi only — albino. Childs 2000, p. 246

mɛlɛkanɔɔ n. (o), pl. mɛlɛkaa — angel. Other forms: mɛlɛkanɔ. Gen 22:12

mɛ̀lɛ̀ŋgàá v. — Southern Kissi only — perceive, know; (mɛ́ɛ́ŋgáá) behold. Other forms: mɛ̀ɛ̀ŋgàà. Childs 2000, p. 246

mɛlɛsoŋnɔ n. (o), pl. mɛlɛsoŋnda — taskmaster, overseer of forced labour. Other forms: mɛlɛsoŋaa. Exod 5:6

mɛlimɛlio v. — let fall here and there. Keita 1979, p. 110

mɛlio v. — make fall; utter (a cry). Other forms: mɛli, mɛlinin. Deut 22:24

mɛllo adj. — left (o ba mɛllo coo, on the left). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): left side. Other forms: mɛl. Gen 13:9

mɛmɛan n. (an) — tears. Ps 42:4

mɛmi v. — make laugh; amuse; make a laughing-stock. Other forms: mɛminin. Gen 21:6

mɛnalanndo v. — make someone swear; swear (to someone), promise on oath. Other forms: mɛnalan. Gen 50:25

mɛnanndo v. — swear, take an oath; oath. Other forms: mɛnan, mɛnannin. Gen 21:24

mɛndul v. — kindle (a fire). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): light, build a fire. Exod 35:3

mɛngɛlaa n. — lookout, watch. Isa 21:8

mɛngɛla v. — lie in wait for, watch secretly, ambush. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): watch secretly, spy on, sneak up on. Hos 13:7

mɛngɔɔ n. — slug, snail. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): slug, freshwater snail. Ps 58:9

mɛnndan n. (an) — water. Other forms: mɛmma. Gen 1:2

mɛ̀ɲjɛ̀ìyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — large measuring cup. Childs 2000, p. 248

mɛ́sɛ́kɛ́ɛ́ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — very thin. Childs 2000, p. 248

mɛ̀sɛ̀làá v. — Southern Kissi only — be small, become thin; reduce (by grouping or piling). Childs 2000, p. 248

mɛ́tɛ́lèíyó n. (o), pl. mɛ́tɛ́lèíyá — Southern Kissi only — teacher. Childs 2000, p. 249

miallo n. (o), pl. mialla — stranger, foreigner. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): guest, visitor, outsider. Gen 23:4

mììlòó v. — Southern Kissi only — shrink, shorten. Childs 2000, p. 249

miinguuo v. — repeat, do again, say again; (miinguu yaŋɔɔlen) lay an ambush. Other forms: miinguu, miinguo, miingul, miingun, miingulnin. Job 33:29

mììŋùùwóŋ n. (ŋ) — Southern Kissi only — rice harvested on a second pass (not ripe the first time). Childs 2000, p. 250

miisuu v. — hurl into the water, engulf, drown; be drowned. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): immerse or dunk in water; also put someone into trouble. Other forms: miisu. Exod 15:1

mîìyó n. (o), pl. mîìláŋ — Southern Kissi only — importance, renown, popularity. Childs 2000, p. 250

milɛɔ n. (o), pl. milɛɛa — mule. Other forms: milɛɛ, milɛaa. 2 Sam 18:9

mílímáláá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — very thick mud. Childs 2000, p. 250

milinndo n. (o) — nose. Other forms: milin. Lev 13:45

milionndo num., pl. milionndan — million. 1 Chr 21:5

mìlóŋ n. (ŋ) — Southern Kissi only — very small hard bead. Childs 2000, p. 250

mímílló n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — large turban worn by Muslims. Childs 2000, p. 250

mingio v. — repair, restore; avenge. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): return, go back; retaliate, replace. Other forms: mingi, minginin, mingin. 2 Chr 34:10

mingullo v. — give back, restore (to someone); repay. Other forms: mingul, mingulnin. Gen 20:7

míŋgímáá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — kind of bee (stings). Childs 2000, p. 250

mìòlló n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — kind of high-forest tree. Childs 2000, p. 250

miolɔɔ v. — swallow. Other forms: miol, mial, mil, mialnin. Ps 88:18

mìòó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — kind of greens for sauce. Childs 2000, p. 250

mìɔ́ɔ́ n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — delivery stage of pregnancy. Childs 2000, p. 250

mìɔ̀ùwó v. — Southern Kissi only — feed (by spoon or hand), force-feed. Childs 2000, p. 251

miɔw v. — be due (pregnancy). Keita 1979, p. 115

mir n. — myrrh. Exod 30:23

mísìkà-mísìkà ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (surface) hairy, rough, bumpy; plump. Childs 2000, p. 251

misiliminɔɔ n. (o) — Muslim. Keita 1979, p. 150

misilio n. (o) — mosque. Keita 1979, p. 150

misimisio n. (o) — anguish, dismay, horror. Ps 55:6

misimisi v. — swallow up, devour. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): plural action of 'swallow'. Gen 41:20

mi conj. — and (then); so that. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): also 'that' (subordinating). Other forms: mí, mì, mó, mò, má, mà. Gen 1:1

m̀-ḿ interj. — Southern Kissi only — no. Childs 2000, p. 251

ḿ-m̀ interj. — Southern Kissi only — yes. Childs 2000, p. 251

mòtóó n. (o), pl. mòtóláŋ — Southern Kissi only — motor, engine. Childs 2000, p. 251

mɔɛi n. (i), pl. mɔɔn — knife; sword. Gen 22:10

mɔ́fíɔ́ɔ́ n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — swollen or fat cheeks. Childs 2000, p. 251

mɔikpɛnɛnɔɔ n. (o) — albino. Keita 1979, p. 161

mɔima vawvan n. — palm wine. Keita 1979, p. 139

mɔiyan n. (an) — wine. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): liquor (generic), spirits. Other forms: mɔima. Gen 9:21

mɔku-mɔku ideo. — entirely (covered). Exod 40:34

mɔ́léí n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — medicine man, Muslim healer (also a man's name). Childs 2000, p. 251

mɔmbillo n. (o) — car, automobile. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): car; also a children's toy car.

mɔ́mndo n. (o) — fog, mist; dew. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): dew, morning mist. 2 Sam 17:12

mɔ́mɔ́ɔ́ n. (o), pl. mɔ́múéí — Southern Kissi only — cooked rice (with sauce on top), food. Childs 2000, p. 251

mɔmtombolaa n. — Pleiades (constellation). Amos 5:8

mɔnɛi n. — grief, sorrow; regret. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): sorrow, sadness; pity, remorse, regret. Other forms: mɔnɛ. Gen 6:6

mɔ̀nííyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — balls of rice flour with lime juice and sugar. Childs 2000, p. 252

mɔ̀nɔ̀ɔ́ n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — philandering. Other forms: mɔ̀nɔ̀ɔ̀. Childs 2000, p. 252

mɔ́ŋtɔ́lɔ́ɔ́ n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — watch (timepiece). Childs 2000, p. 252

mɔ̀ɔ̀bɛ̀íyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — woman's hairstyle; style of hat. Other forms: mɔ̀ɔ̀bɛ̀ɛ́íyo. Childs 2000, p. 252

mɔ́ɔ́ndìɔ̀ŋ-mɔ̀ɔ̀ndìɔ̀ŋ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — soft. Childs 2000, p. 252

mɔ̀ɔ́ɲɔ̀ɔ̀ n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — girl captured by warriors. Childs 2000, p. 252

mɔ̀ɔ̀sàá v. — Southern Kissi only — fold; eat with the folded hand; embrace; put together, mix. Childs 2000, p. 252

mɔɔsa v. — come together, join; (mɔɔsa kpeloo) sleep together, have sexual relations. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): fold; embrace someone; put together, mix. Other forms: mɔɔsu. 2 Sam 12:24

mɔɔsiaa v. — gather; (mɔɔsian) assemble, come together. Other forms: mɔɔsian. Matt 23:37

mɔ́ɔ́sú ideo. — Southern Kissi only — tight, tightly. Childs 2000, p. 252

mɔ̀ɔ̀tííyó n. (o), pl. mɔ̀ɔ̀tííláŋ — Southern Kissi only — car. Childs 2000, p. 252

mɔɔva v. — be engulfed, be covered over; sink (into mud, water). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): be buried, completely covered over. Other forms: mɔɔvaa. Gen 7:19

mɔ̀ɔ̀yɔ́ɔ́ n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — disease causing weakness and severe dizziness. Childs 2000, p. 253

mɔ́ɔ̀yɔ̀ɔ̀ ideo. — utterly (put to shame). Ps 70:3

mɔsillo n. (o) — headgear, turban, cap. Exod 28:4

mɔsɔŋaa v. — gather, put together. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): mix or put together. Keita 1979, p. 110

mɔsɔŋan v. — join together, unite, ally; (mɔsɔŋa) put together, do together. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): mix, combine, put together. Other forms: mɔsɔŋa, mɔsɔŋian, mɔsɔŋannin. Josh 10:6

mɔsɔŋiaa v. — gather (many). Keita 1979, p. 110

mɔ́sɔ́ɔ́ n. (o), pl. mɔ́sɔ̀láŋ — Southern Kissi only — traditional ointment (earth mixed with salt or pepper, for sprains). Other forms: mɔ́sɔ̀ɔ̀. Childs 2000, p. 253

muɛɛn adv. — completely, every one. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): all, completely. Judg 5:31

múɛ̀ɛ̀ŋ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (laugh) softly; (press) firmly. Childs 2000, p. 253

mùɛ̀-fàŋndé n. (i) — Southern Kissi only — war sword (about two feet long). Childs 2000, p. 253

mùɛ̀ìmà-nɛ̀ìyáŋ n. (ma) — Southern Kissi only — whiskey ('strong liquor'). Childs 2000, p. 253

mùɛ̀ìyáŋ n. (ma) — Southern Kissi only — guilt; (cìŋàá mùɛ̀ìyáŋ) plead innocence. Childs 2000, p. 254

muiyo n. (o), pl. muiya — mosquito; gnat. Keita 1979, p. 136

múí ideo. — Southern Kissi only — hard, sharply (of pinching). Childs 2000, p. 254

mulinndo v. — turn (to), go back; do again. Other forms: mulin, mulinin. Jer 23:27

mulio v. — answer; turn. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): turn over; reply. Other forms: muli, mulinin. 2 Sam 14:20

muloo n. (o) — tax, tribute; ransom. 2 Sam 8:2

mulullo v. — answer someone; turn to. Other forms: mulul, mululnin. Gen 45:3

múlúlú ideo. — Southern Kissi only — ground into powder, pulverized. Childs 2000, p. 254

mulumulun v. — roll over, toss and turn, writhe; (mulumulu) roll, turn over. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): roll oneself over; repeat one's words. Other forms: mulumulu. Prov 26:14

mundoo n. (o) — nape of the neck; back. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): nape of the neck. Other forms: mundu. 1 Sam 4:18

mungén adv. — completely, utterly (destroyed, burnt up). Job 1:16

mun det. — these, those (-on plural). Gen 1:14

músúkú ideo. — Southern Kissi only — in small pieces; (sand) fine. Childs 2000, p. 255

mutarde n. — mustard. Matt 13:31

mùùláŋndó v. — Southern Kissi only — put. Childs 2000, p. 255

mùùlɛ̀múúlìáá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — fly bites. Childs 2000, p. 255

muulianndo v. — mix, mingle; join together, combine. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): (noun) a mixture, derived from 'turn'. Other forms: muulian. Exod 30:35

muuluanndo n. (o), pl. muuluannda — hypocrite, deceitful person. Matt 7:5

muuluo v. — turn over, overturn. Keita 1979, p. 110

muungoo v. — return, go back. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): return, go back; also retaliate, replace (variant mùùŋgóó). Other forms: muungu, muungun, muungunin. Gen 3:19

mùúŋndɔ̀ɔ́ adv. — Southern Kissi only — secondly. Childs 2000, p. 255

múúyɔ̀ŋ n. (ŋ) — Southern Kissi only — rice flour of tiny hard grains. Childs 2000, p. 256

nàà ciŋnde n. — toothache. Keita 1979, p. 161

nàà dembe n. — stomach ache, bowel disease. Keita 1979, p. 161

nàà-kìòlèìyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — leprosy, 'cutting sickness'. Childs 2000, p. 257

nàà-kɔ̀ŋjáá n. (o), pl. nàalà-ŋkɔ̀ŋjáláŋ — Southern Kissi only — long illness, usually fatal. Childs 2000, p. 257

nàà malɔɔ n. — sleeping sickness. Keita 1979, p. 161

naamu n., pl. naamula — custom, tradition. John 19:40

naanɔɔ n. — August. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): month around August (literally 'his sickness'). Keita 1979, p. 152

nàá-ó-nàá adv. — Southern Kissi only — everywhere, anywhere, from place to place. Other forms: nàánàá. Childs 2000, p. 258

nàápúm part. — Southern Kissi only — maybe, perhaps; sometimes. Childs 2000, p. 258

nàà siaŋaa n. — leprosy. Keita 1979, p. 161

náàtàtà ideo. — Southern Kissi only — sound of a tree falling in a storm, of strong wind, of twisting wood. Other forms: ŋáàtàtà. Childs 2000, p. 258

-náá part. — Southern Kissi only — very (small) (suffix, only with small or short things). Childs 2000, p. 257

naa pron. — us (independent); our. Gen 1:26

nàà n. (o), pl. naalan — illness, disease. 2 Chr 21:18

nákà-nàkà ideo. — (tremble) violently, all over. Job 21:6

nakɔɔ n. (o), pl. nakɔlan — garden, plantation ; garden, cultivated field, plantation. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): garden (Guéckédou dialect, borrowed from Maninka). Other forms: nakɔ, nakɔla. Gen 2:8

nambaa v. — slip, slide. Keita 1979, p. 110

nàmbàwɛ́íyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — kind of banana. Childs 2000, p. 258

namtalen n. (len) — physical defect, infirmity; paralysis. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): crippled or handicapped person. Deut 15:21

namtanɔɔ n. (o), pl. namtaa — cripple, lame person; person or animal with a physical defect. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): crippled or handicapped person. Lev 21:17

nánde adv. — Southern Kissi only — this year. Other forms: náŋndéè. Childs 2000, p. 258

nanɔɔ v. — pull, draw. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): pull, suck, drag. Other forms: nan, nannin, nennin. Gen 34:3

nanu adv. — here. Gen 15:16

nàŋǎŋndó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — friendship; best friend. Other forms: nàŋáŋndó, nààŋáŋndó. Childs 2000, p. 259

nàŋgàá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — soft mat (used for playing tops); sickness from lack of blood; a woman's hairstyle. Childs 2000, p. 259

naŋɔɔ v. — be good, beautiful, pleasing; goodness, beauty. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): be good, fine, beautiful; be generous, morally good. Other forms: naŋ, naŋnin. Gen 1:4

naŋu v. — bend down, bow (something); (naŋun) lean down, stoop. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): bend, be bent; tip; settle a matter secretly. Other forms: naŋun. Ps 18:10

náŋ adv. — Southern Kissi only — already, once, before; here. Childs 2000, p. 258

nawvo n. (o), pl. nawva — cow, ox; cattle. Other forms: naw, navaa. Gen 12:16

ndààmàá n. — Southern Kissi only — Saturday (formerly the Ndaamaa market day). Other forms: ndàmàá, ndàámáá. Childs 2000, p. 267

ndáámbéíyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — leg stocks. Childs 2000, p. 267

ndaa det. — their. Gen 6:3

ndáà1 part. — Southern Kissi only — together (with them). Childs 2000, p. 267

ndáà2 pron. — they (remote past). Gen 6:3

nda1 conj. — and (between persons). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): also 'with'. Gen 1:21

nda2 pron. — them (independent). Gen 1:21

ndá adv. — Southern Kissi only — there. Childs 2000, p. 266

ndeveiyo n., pl. ndeveila — measure (of capacity), bath. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): small measuring cup. Other forms: ndeveilan. Ezek 45:11

nde n. — mother (term of address, 'Mother!'). 1 Kgs 2:20

ndɛnin adv. — (not) any more, never again. Exod 10:14

ndíámbɔ́ɔ́ n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — young woman. Childs 2000, p. 267

ndíámɔ́ɔ́ n. (o), pl. ndíámɔ́ɔ́wá — Southern Kissi only — friend; young woman. Other forms: ndíáámɔ́ɔ́. Childs 2000, p. 267

ndíɛ́mbɔ̀ n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — term of address for someone younger. Childs 2000, p. 267

ndili adv. — two days after tomorrow. Keita 1979, p. 152

ndíóù-ndíóù ideo. — Southern Kissi only — sound of birds chirping. Childs 2000, p. 268

ndi pron. — it (i class, object). Gen 2:11

ndòndòŋkùó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — cricket (not edible). Childs 2000, p. 268

ndóò pron. — he, she (remote past). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): only a cross-reference to the imperfective suffix -óó. Gen 2:5

ndɔ̀ɔ̀máá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — namesake. Childs 2000, p. 268

ndɔɔ det. — his, her (o class, thing). Gen 1:11

ndɔ det. — his, her (person). Gen 1:27

ndúùlìì adj. — Southern Kissi only — light brown, yellow. Childs 2000, p. 268

nduyɛ conj. — however, indeed. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): and then. Gen 9:4

ndu pron. — him, her (independent). Gen 1:7

néŋèlé-néŋèlé ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (beaten, mashed, pounded) thoroughly, finely. Childs 2000, p. 262

néŋgbè-nèŋgbè- adj. — Southern Kissi only — muddy and flat (shallow swamp that dries up in the dry season). Childs 2000, p. 262

nɛa soalaa n. — latrine, toilet. Keita 1979, p. 142

nɛɛla v. — bolt, bar (a door). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): secure, close or lock properly. 2 Sam 13:17

nɛ́ɛ̀nɛɔ n. (o), pl. nɛ́ɛ̀nɛ́ɛ̀a — sparrow. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): a small red and gray gregarious bird. Matt 10:29

nɛ̀ɛ́ŋndó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — kind of tree (used as firewood). Childs 2000, p. 260

nɛ̀ɛ́1 part. — Southern Kissi only — tag question particle: right?, isn't it?. Other forms: nɛ̌, nɛ́, nɛ̂. Childs 2000, p. 260

nɛ̀ɛ́2 pron. — who?. Gen 1:9

nɛinun v. — displease, be hateful to. Gen 38:10

nɛ̀ìsóó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — bicycle. Childs 2000, p. 261

nɛiyo1 n. (o), pl. nɛilan — path, road. Gen 22:3

nɛiyo2 v. — hurt, be painful; tread, thresh (grain). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): hurt, be in pain; step on, kick, thresh. 2 Kgs 4:19

nɛŋio v. — make prosper, make fruitful; gladden (the heart). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): make something beautiful, make people happy (causative of 'be good'). Other forms: nɛŋi, nɛŋinin, nɛŋul. Gen 39:3

nɛwvo v. — tread, trample, crush underfoot. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): plural of nèìyó 'step on, kick, thresh'. Other forms: nɛw, nɛwnin, nɛwnun. 2 Sam 22:43

nɛyaa adj. — painful, burning; strong (drink); (ɲɛ nɛyaa) pain. Other forms: nɛyan, nɛyaa-nɛyan. Job 33:19

nɛyɔnndo v. — hate; hatred. Other forms: nɛyɔn. Gen 27:41

nɛ part. — focus particle in questions (yɛɛ nɛ … yɛ?). Gen 3:9

ngeemaa n. (o) — scorpion. Luke 10:19

ngeloo n. (o) — carnival. Keita 1979, p. 163

ɲùmícílìó n. (o), pl. ɲùmícílìá — Southern Kissi only — firefly. Childs 2000, p. 282

ɲúmúlúŋ-tùmndóŋ n. — Southern Kissi only — food, cooked rice (slang; lit. 'itchy anus'). Childs 2000, p. 283

piɛiyo v. — pray; ask, beg. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): beg; (benefactive) pray or ask on someone's behalf. Other forms: piɛi. Mark 14:35

piimiaa v. — grow dark, turn black. Other forms: piimiaanin. 1 Kgs 18:45

piindo n. (o), pl. piinda — turtledove. Lev 5:7

piinduu v. — buy (many things), buy up. Gen 47:20

pìíŋndé n. (i) — Southern Kissi only — prerequisites for a magical potion (given at a secret place). Childs 2000, p. 299

piisuu v. — sell (many things), sell off. Other forms: piisuanndo. Matt 13:46

pîìyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — appeal (legal). Childs 2000, p. 299

pii adv. — all night long (lɔl … pii 'spend the whole night …'). Luke 6:12

pìì- adj. — Southern Kissi only — green, unripe. Childs 2000, p. 298

pìkàpìkàá v. — Southern Kissi only — swing a burning stick in the dark to make light. Childs 2000, p. 300

pikiei n. (i), pl. pikion — tent peg, stake; beam (of a loom). Other forms: pikii, pikin. Judg 4:21

pilacieo n. (o), pl. pilacieaa — native, citizen; (pl.) people of the land. Other forms: pilaciee, pilacieea. Lev 17:8

pilannde n. (i) — snuffbox. Keita 1979, p. 159

pilanndo v. — touch. Other forms: pilan. Gen 3:3

pìlàŋndéŋ n. (le) — Southern Kissi only — a species of bamboo. Childs 2000, p. 300

pìlàpílâ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — right away, at once. Childs 2000, p. 300

pila part. — self, -self. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): also 'indeed'. Gen 2:12

pilɛn-pilɛn adv. — one by one, one after another; in pairs. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): one by one; a little, bit by bit. Eccl 7:27

pilɛ num. — one. Gen 1:9

pílíkò-pílíkò ideo. — Southern Kissi only — one after another (things passing in a series). Childs 2000, p. 301

pìlìŋàá v. — Southern Kissi only — spoil (a child). Childs 2000, p. 301

pílí-pílí ideo. — Southern Kissi only — extremely (high, far, long). Childs 2000, p. 301

pìllá adv. — Southern Kissi only — very much, a lot. Childs 2000, p. 301

pílò ideo. — Southern Kissi only — nearly, very closely (just missing). Childs 2000, p. 301

pîm ideo. — Southern Kissi only — thudding sound (pounding, falling, a blow). Childs 2000, p. 301

pìndàpìndàá v. — Southern Kissi only — wrap around, twine (thread on a spindle). Childs 2000, p. 302

pìndìèí n. (i), pl. pìndìóŋ — Southern Kissi only — sluggishness, listlessness, laziness. Childs 2000, p. 302

pindo n. — surroundings; (… pindo) around. Gen 19:4

pìndùlló v. — Southern Kissi only — roll cotton thread on a stick (spinning). Childs 2000, p. 303

piɔmndo n. (o), pl. piɔmnda — idol, image (of a god). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): small carved stone figure (nomoli) kept for an ancestor spirit. Exod 32:4

poondiaa v. — carry off (as plunder, captive), take away, confiscate. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): take away (plural action); shuck. Num 14:3

poo n. (o), pl. poaa — son, (male) child; (pl.) sons, descendants. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): boy, youth. Other forms: po. Gen 4:25

pòtómánɔ̀ɔ́ n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — initiate boy (in bush school). Childs 2000, p. 308

pɔ́lɔ̀kɔ̀pɔ́lɔ̀kɔ̀ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — thoroughly mixed, muddy (consistency). Childs 2000, p. 308

pùlàléŋ n. (le) — Southern Kissi only — line, column (of people, ants); ancestral line. Childs 2000, p. 311

pùlóó n. (o), pl. pùlúláŋ — Southern Kissi only — cluster, pod (kola nuts, palm nuts). Childs 2000, p. 311

pulɔɔ v. — wash (people, body). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): wash, bathe. Other forms: pulu, pilu. Gen 18:4

pulta n., pl. pultan — ash. Exod 9:8

púŋ1 ideo. — (idiiyo púŋ) very early in the morning. Gen 19:27

púŋ2 ideo. — Southern Kissi only — suddenly. Childs 2000, p. 313

pùùlùnɔ̀ɔ́ n. (o), pl. pùùlùá — Southern Kissi only — European, white person; someone following Western ways. Childs 2000, p. 314

pùùlù- adj. — Southern Kissi only — foreign, European, Western, modern; governmental. Childs 2000, p. 313

puundulen n. (len), pl. puundun — root. Other forms: puundule. Keita 1979, p. 140

puusiaa v. — scatter, disperse. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): scatter, spread about. Other forms: puusian. Gen 11:8

puusianɔɔ n. (o) — reactionary (Keita). Keita 1979, p. 148

pùùsóó n. (o), pl. pùùsúláŋ — Southern Kissi only — termite hill. Childs 2000, p. 314

púúwɔ́ɔ́ n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — goat-like animal. Childs 2000, p. 315

púvɔ́ɔ́ n. (o), pl. púwvɛa — gazelle, deer. Other forms: púvɛ. Deut 14:5
