saasa n. — cage. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): basket for holding chickens, chicken coop. Ezek 19:9

sáátátá ideo. — Southern Kissi only — straight on, right at. Childs 2000, p. 317

sálábú ideo. — Southern Kissi only — stretched out straight. Childs 2000, p. 319

sâlló n. (o), pl. sâllá — Southern Kissi only — a fish species (shark?). Childs 2000, p. 319

sámàá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — credit, charge. Childs 2000, p. 319

tɛɛmbua adj. — destroying, destroyer. Exod 12:13

tɛɛmbuula n., pl. tɛɛmbuulan — transgressions, offences. Lev 16:21

tɛɛmbuuo v. — destroy; break, transgress (a law). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): plural of tàmbéí 'be ruined': spoil, break, misuse. Other forms: tɛɛmbuu, tɛɛmbuunin. Gen 6:7

tɛɛndanndo v. — despise, look down on, scorn. Other forms: tɛɛndan. Gen 16:4

tɛɛndiaa v. — split, burst open; split apart (earth). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): split; divide, distribute; show one by one. Other forms: tɛɛndiaanin, tɛɛndian. Isa 24:19

tɛ̀ɛ̀ndo n. (o) — scalp ringworm, scall. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): ringworm. Lev 13:30

tɛɛnduuo v. — hatch (eggs). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): hatch eggs. Isa 59:5

tɛ́ɛ́nɛí n. — small stone, grain (of dust). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): small rock or stone; ten large sheaves of rice. Prov 8:26

tɛɛngaa v. — convey, carry across; deliver (a message). 2 Kgs 9:4

tɛɛngei n. (i), pl. tɛɛngon — hole, breach, hollow. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): hole; burrow (of a rat or squirrel). Judg 15:19

tɛɛngullo v. — tell, report (to someone). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): take (someone) across for someone. Other forms: tɛɛngul. Gen 45:26

tɛɛnguuo v. — take across, make (many) cross. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): cross with or carry across (a river); plural of tàŋɔ̀ɔ́ 'cross'. Other forms: tɛɛnguu. Gen 32:24

tɛɛnɔn n. — gravel. Keita 1979, p. 155

tɛɛnuu v. — clear (a way), clear of vegetation. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): clear an area of large vegetation for cultivation. Isa 40:3

tɛɛn postp. — between, among. Gen 1:6

tɛɛsiaa v. — interpret, explain. Gen 40:8

tɛɛsial v. — interpret, explain (to someone). Gen 41:12

tɛilullo v. — stretch out, spread (the hands) to; offer (the cheek) to. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): spread out (e.g. to dry) for someone; open one's hands to someone. Other forms: tɛilul, tɛilu. Isa 65:2

tɛiye n. — confluence; shoot, sprout; branch of a river, stream. Other forms: tɛyii, tɛyun, tɛiyun. Isa 11:1

tɛi n. (i) — groundnut, peanut. Keita 1979, p. 140

tɛ̀i v. — spread out (in the sun, to dry). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): spread, esp. in the sun to dry; spread one's hands or legs apart. 2 Sam 17:19

tɛ́kpɛ́-tɛ́kpɛ́ adv. — one by one, individually (counting). Num 1:2

tɛ̂lɛ́kɛ̀lɛ́ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (smooth, like cement). Childs 2000, p. 356

tɛlɛlɔɔ n. — surface. Keita 1979, p. 155

tɛndaa v. — split, divide; (with seilen) testify. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): split, cut open. Other forms: tɛnda, tɛndanin. Lev 5:1

tɛndanɔɔ n. (o) — surgeon. Keita 1979, p. 145

tɛngɛlen n. (len) — reed. Job 40:26

tɛ́ngɛ̀ n. — lamp, torch. Other forms: tɛngɛla. Prov 24:20

tɛu n. — termite mound. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): chaff, rice straw left after threshing. Keita 1979, p. 137

tìàá v. — Southern Kissi only — state the facts directly; have recently gone somewhere. Childs 2000, p. 358

tiamaa n. — flirtation, seduction; (vanalanɔ tiamaa) loose woman, seductress. Other forms: tiamaalan. Prov 7:5

tìàmùùwó v. — Southern Kissi only — chew. Childs 2000, p. 358

tììfàá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — gate at the entrance of the bush school. Childs 2000, p. 358

tiilaa v. — besiege, surround. Other forms: tiila. Deut 20:19

tiilanndo adj. — round, circular. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): (verb) be round or full; curve, swirl. Other forms: tiilannde, tiilannda, tiilanndan. 1 Kgs 7:23

tíílíó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — biting fly. Childs 2000, p. 358

tiimbuuo v. — loosen (hair); take off (ornaments). Other forms: tiimbuu, tiimbun. Num 5:18

tiindaa v. — make firm, confirm; lean (one's hand on). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): step on, press with the feet or hands, press against. Other forms: tiinda. 1 Chr 17:24

tiindanndo v. — trust in, rely on. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): depend on, trust (middle of 'step on, press'). Other forms: tiindan. Ps 43:5

tííndííyo n. — heel (bɛngu tííndííyo). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): heel, ankle. Other forms: tííndíí. Gen 3:15

tiiyaa v. — reach, arrive at; be enough. Other forms: tiiya, tiiyanin. Gen 3:22

tiiyallo v. — bring to, deliver to; proclaim (news) to. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): go somewhere for someone. Other forms: tiiyal. Acts 8:40

tíkítíkí ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (firmly stuck). Childs 2000, p. 360

timbio v. — untie, loosen; fulfil (a vow). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): also: explain. Other forms: timbi. Luke 19:30

tindaa n. (o), pl. tindalan — staff, walking stick ; staff, rod. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): cane, walking stick. Other forms: tinda, tindala. Exod 4:2

tindilen n. (len) — pillar, column. Other forms: tindile. Exod 13:21

tindima n. — waves, billows. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): a place with a fast current, rapids in a river. Other forms: tindian. Job 9:8

tindi1 n., pl. tindila — scar (of a boil, burn); (pl.) marks. Lev 13:23

tindi2 v. — wake (someone); raise (from the dead). John 12:17

tingɔɔ v. — gather (firewood). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): gather, fetch; also cut, break (wood). Other forms: tingu. 1 Kgs 17:10

tiŋio adj. — black, dark. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): black, dark; also dark blue. Other forms: tiŋi, tiŋia, tiŋii. Song 1:5

tiŋndo n. — island; distance, space (between two places). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): a measure of distance, roughly a mile; also a demijohn bottle. Gen 30:36

tìŋndó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — argument or palaver started for no reason. Childs 2000, p. 361

tìŋɔ̀léŋ n. (le), pl. tìŋɔ̀láŋ — Southern Kissi only — awl. Childs 2000, p. 361

tíŋɔ́ŋ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (dumbstruck, unable to answer). Childs 2000, p. 361

tiŋɔɔ v. — provoke, put to the test; harass. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): pledge, vow; also start an argument without provocation. Exod 17:2

tíŋtíŋ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (sound of a guitar or string instrument). Childs 2000, p. 361

tiŋ adv. — a little, slightly; some, a few. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): (adj.) some, a few; (adv.) a little, slightly. Other forms: tíŋ. Gen 18:2

tìɲàá v. — Southern Kissi only — squeeze out the last drop. Childs 2000, p. 360

tiondɔɔ v. — wake up, awake. Other forms: tiondu, tiandu, tindu, tiandunin. Gen 41:7

tíó n. — Southern Kissi only — disobedience, unruliness. Childs 2000, p. 361

tiɔmɔɔ v. — join, unite; (tiɔm balan) clap one's hands; (tiɔmɔɔ a) have sexual relations with. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): card or comb cotton; clap hands, snap fingers; flirt, make love (esp. adulterously). Other forms: tiɔm. Ps 47:2

tiɔn num. — two. Other forms: ŋiɔn, ŋiin, miɔn, miun, miunndon. Gen 1:6

tìɔ̀ɔ́ n. (o), pl. tèèláŋ — Southern Kissi only — responsibility, blame. Childs 2000, p. 362

tisaa v. — pursue, attack; urge on, hurry (someone). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): stumble, fall down; also jump on, assault; follow; bear witness. Other forms: tisa, tisanin. Gen 14:7

tìsàá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — penile sheath of bamboo fibre (after circumcision). Childs 2000, p. 359

tìsáá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — narrow part of a trail. Childs 2000, p. 362

tíú ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (round, curvaceous). Childs 2000, p. 362

tivaa n. — whole extent, entire surface; (o tivaa sɔ́) all over.

tivolla n. — jackals. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): a wild dog-like animal ('fox'). Other forms: tivoli, tivolaa. Isa 13:22

tiwba v. — be able to, can. Neh 8:3

tìwììyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — bush devil, bush spirit. Childs 2000, p. 363

tìwùèìyó n. — Southern Kissi only — eyebrow liner (black powder). Childs 2000, p. 363

tiw v. — be enough, have room for; master, overcome. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): spread throughout; be enough, suffice; fit. Gen 13:6

tì ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (underscores smallness). Childs 2000, p. 358

toal v. — come down (upon). Other forms: toalnin. Gen 11:5

toandaa v. — stretch out, spread (cloth, net). Isa 40:22

toaŋaa v. — bake (flat bread), parch (grain). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): fry, cook. Other forms: toaŋ, toaŋan. 2 Sam 13:8

tódǎŋ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — fully. Childs 2000, p. 363

tofaa v. — look at, see. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): also: inspect, taste, search, find out. Other forms: tofa, tofanin. Gen 6:12

tofanndo n. (o), pl. tofanndan — mirror; looking. Jas 1:23

tofan v. — look back; look to. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): look at oneself (in a mirror). Gen 19:17

tòkpùéí n. (i), pl. tòkpòóŋ — Southern Kissi only — thick-skinned palm nut. Childs 2000, p. 363

tólítólí ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (rapid flow, gushing). Childs 2000, p. 363

tòlòmàá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — slow-moving cat-like fruit-eating animal (potto?). Childs 2000, p. 364

tolɔɔ v. — go down, descend. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): descend, climb or slide down. Other forms: tol, toal, tul, toalnin, tulnin. Gen 8:3

tomaa n. (o) — old man (Keita). Keita 1979, p. 148

tòmbàá n. — Southern Kissi only — cassava cooked before pounding. Childs 2000, p. 364

tombolaa v. — join, couple; tell, recount. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): talk, discuss, explain; join together, line up. Other forms: tombola, tombolal. Gen 40:9

tómbólàá n. — Southern Kissi only — money or food offered to the dead. Childs 2000, p. 364

tomboliaa v. — join together, sew together (many pieces). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): line up things or people; talk in sequence. Exod 26:14

tómbólóó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — fleas (esp. in clothes). Childs 2000, p. 364

tòmbòmɛ́sɔ́ɔ́ n. — Southern Kissi only — tree-like plant species. Childs 2000, p. 365

tombon n. — high places (shrines). 1 Kgs 13:33

tòmbòó1 n. — Southern Kissi only — waist area (where women keep a small purse). Childs 2000, p. 364

tòmbòó2 n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — object tied into a woman's wrapper, kept hidden. Childs 2000, p. 365

tómbòó n. (o), pl. tómbòláŋ — Southern Kissi only — secret society of men and women (members disrobe). Childs 2000, p. 365

tómbòsìɔ́ n. (o), pl. tómbòsìá — Southern Kissi only — tiny rat, hero of folk tales (Tombose). Childs 2000, p. 365

tóndóó n. — furnace, kiln. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): blacksmith's furnace; also the base of elephant grass; a young cow. Other forms: tóndó. Dan 3:23

tondɔɔ v. — set up, pitch (a tent); hang (a curtain). Other forms: tondu, tondunin. Exod 40:2

tongei n. — width, breadth; handbreadth, span. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): (adjective) wide (from tɔ̀ŋɔ̀ɔ́ 'widen'). Other forms: tongii. 1 Kgs 7:23

tongo cɔwvo n. (o) — forge, smithy. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): lit. 'war hut': the smithy, where the weapons were made. Keita 1979, p. 142

tongo n. — porch, hall. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): village hall, open roofed meeting house. Acts 3:11

tongu v. — be wide, spacious; broaden. Neh 7:4

tòŋgó-máàŋndó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — small wall-less hut at the village entrance where elders address the ancestors. Childs 2000, p. 365

toŋɔɔ v. — fry, bake (cakes). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): fry, cook. Other forms: toŋ. Jer 7:18

tóŋtóŋndéŋ n. (le) — Southern Kissi only — water droplets. Childs 2000, p. 366

toɲaa n. (o) — truth; justice. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): truth; kindness, goodness, a favour. Gen 42:16

tòòlóó n. (o), pl. tòòlóláŋ — Southern Kissi only — disease, possibly tetanus, from stepping on something. Childs 2000, p. 366

tooluo v. — arrange, repair; provide for. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): assist, help. Other forms: toolu, toolunin. Keita 1979, p. 113

toomaa n. (o) — circumcision. Other forms: tooma. Gen 17:10

tóómá-bòndóó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — girls' initiation society (Sande). Childs 2000, p. 367

tooma pɔɔndo n. — tattoos. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): boys' initiation society (Poro). Keita 1979, p. 144

toongoo n. (o) — nephew, niece (sister's child). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): nephew, sister's son. Gen 29:12

toosiaa v. — make, prepare; repair (Keita). Other forms: toosian, toosial. Gen 1:16

toosial v. — make, prepare for (someone). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): fix, make, dress (someone) for someone. Gen 2:18

toosian v. — be made, prepared (of). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): get prepared; get dressed. Gen 19:3

tootoo adv. — low; humbly; in a whisper. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): underscores how low (ideophone). 1 Sam 2:7

toovaa n. (o) — bull. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): male animal (cow, sheep, etc.), bull. Keita 1979, p. 137

toovio n. (o), pl. toovia — he-goat, billy goat. Gen 37:31

too n. — south (a ba too 'southward'). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): low, lower part, below, down; also Monrovia (down-country). Gen 12:9

tosaa v. — do, make. Other forms: tosa, tosanin, tosan, tosal. Gen 2:5

tosalan v. — happen to (someone). Gen 44:29

tosallo v. — do for, do to (someone). Other forms: tosal, tosalnin. Gen 9:24

tosanndo v. — happen, come about; be done. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): be done, be made; succeed. Other forms: tosan, tosannin. Gen 6:11

tova adj. — male (of cattle). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): male (cow, sheep, etc.), bull. Other forms: tovaa. Exod 29:1

tovɔɔ v. — drive out, expel; pursue; dig (a well). Other forms: toaw, toawnin, townun. Gen 3:23

tòwàá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — belly harp, guitar. Childs 2000, p. 368

tɔ̀a det. — the others. Gen 4:15

tɔ́kpɔ̀ɔ́ n. (o), pl. tɔ́kpùá — Southern Kissi only — tailless baboon; clan whose taboo is the baboon. Childs 2000, p. 368

tɔ̀làá v. — Southern Kissi only — tap a palm tree for palm wine. Childs 2000, p. 368

tɔ̀lnɔ̀ɔ́ n. (o), pl. tɔ̀llá — Southern Kissi only — member of a clan or lineage. Childs 2000, p. 368

tɔ̀lóó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — private parts, genital area. Childs 2000, p. 368

tɔ́lɔ́lɔ́ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (smooth, like an animal's hair). Childs 2000, p. 368

tɔlɔɔ1 n. (o), pl. tɔlɔɔlan — plant. Exod 10:5

tɔlɔɔ2 v. — plant; plant, tree. Other forms: tɔl, tɔal, tɔalnin. Exod 10:5

tɔmndo n. (o), pl. tɔmnda — monkey. Keita 1979, p. 137

tɔndaa v. — weave, warp (thread). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): make the warp thread for weaving, wrap spools; also defame someone. Other forms: tɔnda. Isa 19:9

tɔndikɔɔliei n. (i), pl. tɔndikɔɔlion — tendon, hamstring. Keita 1979, p. 132

tɔ́ndɔɔ num. — tenth; tithe. Lev 27:32

tɔnɔɔ n. (o) — profit, benefit; interest (on a loan). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): gain, profit; good fortune. Other forms: tɔnɔ. Prov 3:14

tɔ̀ŋâŋndó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — nocturnal bird species, calling 'tɔŋ … tɔŋ'. Childs 2000, p. 369

tɔ́ŋgɔ́tɔ́ŋgáá n. — Southern Kissi only — a traditional medicine. Childs 2000, p. 369

tɔŋndo n. (o), pl. tɔŋndan — law, commandment, order. Other forms: tɔŋ, tɔŋnda. Gen 2:16

tɔ́ŋndó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — fine for being late to communal work. Childs 2000, p. 369

tɔ̀ɲàá v. — Southern Kissi only — speak quickly; repeat what someone said. Childs 2000, p. 368

tɔɔmaa n. — monster, monstrous beast (visi tɔɔmaa). Other forms: tɔɔma. Rev 13:1

tɔɔmaseloo n. (o) — sign, mark. Other forms: tɔɔmasele. Gen 9:12

tɔɔndan v. — test, try; tempt; attempt. Other forms: tɔɔndanndo. Gen 22:1

tɔ̀ɔ̀ɲá v. — Southern Kissi only — do quickly, speak very fast, eat or pound rapidly. Childs 2000, p. 369

tɔ́ɔ́yaa n. — blame, fault, responsibility (bii X tɔ́ɔ́yaa 'hold X responsible, blame X'). Rom 9:19

tɔɔ v. — wash (things, clothes), rinse. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): wash clothes, launder. Gen 6:4

tɔ́ɔ́ n., pl. tɔ́ɔ́lan — fame, renown, reputation; news, report. Gen 6:4

tɔ́ num. — ten. Gen 5:8

túdú ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (short, small). Childs 2000, p. 370

tueiyo v. — wash, rinse (the inside of vessels). Matt 23:25

tùèndɔ̀ɔ́ n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — a musical instrument. Childs 2000, p. 371

tueyɔɔ v. — hear, listen; learn (news). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): also: understand; sense, perceive, smell. Other forms: tuei, tuɛi, tui, tuɛinin. Gen 3:8

tue n. — drop; (tue-tue) drop by drop. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): (ideophone) sound of water falling a drop at a time. Jer 3:3

tuɛi v. — roast (meat). Exod 12:8

tuɛndɔɔ n. — chisel, engraving tool. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): a blacksmith's chisel for cutting iron. Jer 17:1

túfɛ́-túfɛ́ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (sweet-tasting). Childs 2000, p. 371

tufɔɔ v. — spit. Other forms: tufu. Deut 25:9

tuilian n. (an) — urine. Other forms: tuilima. Keita 1979, p. 132

tuinɔnndo v. — show favour, have mercy (tuinun … iɲíí). Other forms: tuinun. Matt 18:33

tuiŋio v. — take out of the fire, snatch from the fire. Other forms: tuiŋi. Jude 1:23

tuisinndo v. — humble oneself, submit. Other forms: tuisin. Gen 16:9

tuisio v. — bring down, send (rain, calamity) upon; humble. Other forms: tuisi, tuisinin. Gen 2:5

tuituiyaa v. — folded, rolled up. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): fold together, roll up (plural of tùwɔ̀ɔ́ 'fold'). John 20:7

tùkpàá n. (o), pl. tùkpàláŋ — Southern Kissi only — cannon, mortar; celebratory gunshot (at wakes). Childs 2000, p. 372

tullo n. (o) — top, summit. Exod 24:17

tuma conj. — when, at the time when. Gen 2:4

tùmbáfùíyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — bathtub. Childs 2000, p. 372

tumbé n. — wrath, fury. Isa 54:8

túmbúlnɔ̀ɔ́ n. (o), pl. túmbúllá — Southern Kissi only — exorcist, ritual cleanser (after a taboo is broken). Childs 2000, p. 373

tumbu n., pl. tumbulan — sheaf. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): a large sheaf of rice. Other forms: tumbula. Gen 37:7

tumndo n., pl. tumnda — base, foot, socket; stock (of a vine); (pl.) vineyards. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): bottom, base, background; buttocks, anus; palm nut head. Gen 40:9

tumulɛi adj. — rotten, putrid, unclean. Other forms: tumulɛiyon, tumulɛin. Lev 19:7

tumulu v. — rot, putrefy, become foul. Other forms: tumulnin. Ps 38:6

tum yekpandio n. — rifle butt. Keita 1979, p. 156

tuncua n. — puppy. Keita 1979, p. 137

tùndòó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — bent stick (animal trap; holder for palm cutters). Childs 2000, p. 373

tundɔɔ v. — bend, twist; pervert (justice, words); oppress. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): bend or curve. Other forms: tundan. Job 8:3

tundun v. — bow down, prostrate oneself. Ps 95:6

tundu v. — bow (the face to the ground). Gen 17:3

tunndo n. (o), pl. tunnda — dog. Exod 11:7

tuŋndo v. — fry, bake (cakes) for (someone). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): fry for someone (benefactive of tòŋɔ̀ɔ́ 'fry'). Jer 44:19

túŋòó n. (o), pl. túŋòá — Southern Kissi only — midget, dwarf. Childs 2000, p. 374

túŋótúŋóó n. (o), pl. túŋótúŋúá — Southern Kissi only — large grasshopper. Childs 2000, p. 374

tuŋɔɔ v. — deprive of, withhold (from someone). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): be greedy; deprive someone of something by keeping it for oneself. Job 22:7

tuŋ adv. — always, continually. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): only, just. Other forms: tuŋ-tuŋ. Gen 6:5

tùsìó v. — Southern Kissi only — be dirty. Childs 2000, p. 374

tùúlen n. — a little, a small amount, (just) enough. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): being enough, sufficient. Prov 15:16

tuuliaala n. — carved figures, images, idols. Deut 4:23

tuuliaa v. — carve, engrave, embroider (figures). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): imitate, gesticulate; make illustrations. 1 Kgs 6:29

tuulianɔɔ n. (o) — draughtsman. Keita 1979, p. 145

tuuloo v. — heat up, flare up; (tuulu kɔl) become angry. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): be warm, become hot, heat; also beat. Other forms: tuulu, tuulunin. Gen 31:36

tuulul v. — measure out (to someone); show (a pattern) to. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): measure for someone. Other forms: tuululnin. Luke 6:38

tuunduanndo adj. — crooked, winding; perverse (conduct). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): bend over, be bent (middle plural of 'bend'). Other forms: tuunduanndan, tuunduan. Prov 28:6

tuunduɛiyo adj. — crooked, twisted; perverse, crafty. Other forms: tuunduɛiyan, tuundɛilan. Prov 10:9

tuunduuvo v. — make crooked, confuse (a path). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): bend many things (plural of 'bend'). Isa 3:12

tuuŋanndan v. — compare oneselves with one another. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): compare, make comparisons. 2 Cor 10:12

tùúpá conj. — Southern Kissi only — until, before. Childs 2000, p. 375

tuusu v. — go down; extend (border). 1 Sam 25:1

tuuvo v. — measure; plan. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): plan (middle of tùùwó 'measure'). Ezek 40:5

tùùwó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — male genitals. Childs 2000, p. 376

tuvaa n., pl. tuvaala — measure, measuring unit; (pl.) weights and measures; (yoole tuvaalen) measuring line. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): (verb) measure, take the size of; decide. Other forms: tuvaalen. Exod 16:36

tuvɔɔ v. — draw back, fold back (the arm). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): fold, fold around, wrap; bury; embrace; sprain. Josh 8:26

tuwvo adj. — hot, burning; (kɔl tuwvo) anger, wrath. Other forms: tuwve, tuwvon. Exod 32:10

tù ideo. — Southern Kissi only — all, entirely. Childs 2000, p. 370

docs.title: V
docs.text:
vaalɛiyan adj. — sour (mɔima vaalɛiyan 'vinegar'). Luke 23:36

vaaliaa v. — turn sour; (of teeth) be set on edge; be bitter. Jer 31:29

vaalio adv. — now, nowadays; present (vanndacieea vaalio ho 'this generation'). Matt 11:16

vaan-vaan adj. — fine, thin (cloth): kola vaan-vaan 'veil'.

vaasan n. — cuts, gashes (on the body, in mourning). Lev 19:28

vaa1 n. — kind, sort (vaa lende 'of that kind, such'). Gen 39:9

vaa2 num., pl. vàálan — thousand. Gen 1:16

vaa3 v. — farm, plough. Other forms: vee, veenin. Keita 1979, p. 115

vaa4 v. — be. Other forms: co, va. Gen 1:16

vakpa adv. — clearly, openly, in plain view. Phil 3:15

valaa n., pl. valalan — mat; pallet, bed. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): (sleeping) mat. Other forms: vala. Acts 5:15

vallo n. (o), pl. valtan — work, labour. Other forms: vali, valta, vallon. Gen 2:2

valoo n. — drought, dry weather, absence of rain. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): a short dry spell, a break in the rains. Hag 1:11

vanabɛnduyɛi n. — greatness, majesty, glory; leadership. Ps 104:1

vanabolofaa n. (o) — rich person. Keita 1979, p. 149

vanacamndo n. (o) — magician. Keita 1979, p. 145

vanacieeyɛi n. (i) — humanity, humaneness (Keita). Keita 1979, p. 149

vanacieo n. (o), pl. vanndacieea — human being, man; (pl.) people, mankind. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): citizen, human being. Other forms: vanaciee, vanndaciee. Gen 1:26

vanaikɔɔ n. (o) — poor person. Keita 1979, p. 149

vanakaa n. (o) — dyer. Keita 1979, p. 145

vanakɛndɛyɛi n. (i) — kindness, goodness. Prov 11:17

vana lacòòva n. — liar. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): lie, falsehood. Keita 1979, p. 149

vanalanɔɔ n. (o) — woman, female person. Gen 1:27

vanaɲɛcaa n. (o) — musician. Keita 1979, p. 145

vanapɔnɔɔ n. (o) — man, male person. Gen 1:27

vanapɔnɔyɛi n. — manliness, courage (tosa vanapɔnɔyɛi 'be brave, act like men'). 1 Sam 4:9

vanasialaa n. (o) — carpenter. Keita 1979, p. 145

vana-solia-lasálàá n., pl. vanaa-solia-lasálàá — priest. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): people involved in initiation ceremonies. Other forms: vana-solia-lasálà. Gen 41:45

vana tambɛiyo n. — disabled person, cripple. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): poverty. Keita 1979, p. 149

vana-vana pron. — anyone; (neg.) no one. Gen 2:25

vanayɛi n. (i) — kinship, relatives. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): relative, member of the same family. Gen 13:8

vana pron., pl. vanaa — the one who, someone (head of a relative clause); person. Gen 2:9

vangala v. — multiply, make numerous. Deut 10:22

vanlaandoo n. (o), pl. vanlaandua — woman, female person; (pl.) women. Other forms: vanlaandu. Gen 14:16

vanndo n. (o), pl. vannda — person, human being. Other forms: van. Gen 27:42

vannun v. — be, remain, dwell. Ezek 16:49

vanpiaandua n. — men, male persons. Other forms: vanpiaandu. Gen 10:21

vaŋ ideo. — (ideophone) completely; bright red (lasiaŋa vaŋ, diw vaŋ). Isa 1:18

vawvo n. (o), pl. vawvan — oil palm; palm tree. Song 7:9

vayia v. — tread, press (grapes); tread down (soil). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): wring, squeeze (e.g. cloth). Gen 40:11

va v. — be (past); past progressive auxiliary. Other forms: ve, vanin. Gen 1:2

veeliaa v. — dry up (waters, rivers). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): dry up (plural of wèlàá 'become dry'). Other forms: veeliaanin. Isa 42:15

veeloo v. — call ; call; call upon. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): call, name. Other forms: veelu, veelunin. Gen 3:9

veelɔnndo v. — be called, be named. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): call oneself. Rom 2:17

veeluanndo v. — call one another. Keita 1979, p. 114

veelul v. — call (someone) for (someone), summon. Num 22:5

veesiaa v. — make dry, wither. Gen 41:6

velaa v. — dry up, recede (water). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): become dry (of water). Other forms: vela, velanin. Gen 8:1

velanndo v. — dry up (Keita); likeness, meaning (Bible). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): resemble. Keita 1979, p. 114

velan n. (lan) — image, likeness. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): resemblances (from wèlǎŋndó 'resemble'). Gen 1:26

vellaa-velle pron. — one another, each other. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): (adverb) together. Gen 11:3

velun v. — be born. John 3:6

velu v. — beget, father. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): bear, give birth, be born; resemble (the stem wélù is used of a father siring). Gen 5:4

vennun v. — take refuge, escape, flee to safety; escape (the notice of). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): hide oneself. Prov 22:3

vesaa v. — dry, be dry. Other forms: vesa, vesanin. Job 18:16

veselɛilen adj. — arid, desert (lɛŋnde veselɛilen 'desert, wilderness'). Other forms: veselɛile. Josh 8:15

vesɛiyo adj. — dry; hard; dry land. Other forms: vesɛi, vesɛiya, vesɛilan, vesɛilen. Gen 1:9

vesul v. — sprinkle. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): splash. Lev 4:6

vɛɛnnden n. (len) — nest. Job 39:27

vɛ̀ɛ̀ part. — yes/no question marker; how?. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): what? why? how? how much?. Gen 15:8

vɛlɛ adv. — again, also. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): also 'more, else, extra'. Gen 1:6

vɛ adv. — why?. Gen 24:31

viamaa v. — send (someone). Other forms: viam, vim, viamnin. 2 Sam 12:1

viannan adj. — hidden, secret; of refuge. Other forms: viannanndo, viannannda, viannanndon. Deut 4:43

viiku v. — miscarry, cast young; (noun) untimely birth. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): miscarry, abort; also lose a spouse through death. Other forms: vííkù. Gen 31:38

vííyo n. (o), pl. vííya — orphan. Deut 24:17

vii v. — stone (vii … a powtan). Exod 17:4

vilɛi-vilɛi adj. — very tall, huge; (vanaa vilɛi-vilɛiya) giants. Other forms: vilɛi-vilɛiya, vilɛi-vilɛiye, vilɛi-vilɛiyo, vilɛi-vilɛiyon. Gen 6:4

vílɛ́iyo n. (o), pl. vílɛ́iya — dead person, corpse. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): (adjective) dead, deceased. Other forms: vílɛ́i. Gen 23:3

vilɛi adj. — long, high, tall. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): long, tall, sharp. Other forms: vilɛiye, vilɛilan. Matt 17:1

vilio v. — carry (loads), transport; lead, conduct. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): carry loads, haul, draw (plural of 'bear, carry'). Other forms: vili. Num 4:24

vilul v. — bear (a child) to someone. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): deliver (a child) for someone, as a midwife. Gen 30:7

violɔɔ v. — give birth. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): bear (a child). Other forms: vialu, vialunin. Gen 6:1

vionnɔnndo v. — hide oneself; refuge. Other forms: vionnun, viannun. Gen 3:8

vionɔɔ v. — hide (something). Other forms: vian, vin. Exod 2:2

viovɔɔ v. — put, throw, cast. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): stay in one place for a long time; (benefactive) throw away. Other forms: viow, viaw, viawnin. Dan 3:20

viɔw v. — knock, strike; shoot. Other forms: viɔ, via. Num 35:22

visiei n. (i) — flesh, meat. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): meat. Gen 2:21

visio n. (o), pl. visia — animal. Gen 1:21

viw v. — last long, linger, delay. Other forms: viwnin, viwanin. Jer 29:28

volion n. — silver, money. Other forms: volin, volii, voliei. Gen 13:2

volio v. — shine, flash; (of lightning) flash. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): (noun) lightning. Other forms: voli, volinin. Exod 19:16

vólotótoo adj., pl. vólotótolan — scarlet. Exod 26:1

volɔɔ n. (o), pl. volɔɔlan — load, burden; garment, clothing (volɔɔ cuɛinan 'garment'). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): tool, implement; (pl.) loads. Other forms: volɔɔla. Lev 11:32

vomɔɔ v. — send (someone), dispatch; charge, command. Other forms: viomɔɔ, viomnun. Gen 37:13

vomullo v. — spin (thread); (vomulaa) spinner, spindle. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): spin cotton, weave. Other forms: vomul, vomulaa. Exod 35:25

vóólun-vóólunndo n. — tumult, uproar, clamour. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): (base verb) start from fright, tremble with fear. Other forms: vóólun-vóólun, vóólun-vóólunn. 1 Sam 4:14

vooluo v. — startle; take by surprise, fall upon. Other forms: voolu, voolunin. Keita 1979, p. 114

voosanndo n. (o) — sprain. Keita 1979, p. 162

voosu n. — fig. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): fig tree; also a fern-like plant. Other forms: voosun. Luke 13:6

vosɛ interj. — greetings (to several people): la vosɛ!. Keita 1979, p. 21

vowlul v. — put (into), fill for (someone); throw to; (vowlul X sondo) answer X. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): dress someone, put (clothes) on someone; put in for someone. Other forms: vowlulnin, vowlu. Gen 44:1

vownun v. — put on (clothes, sandals). Exod 12:11

vowvo v. — put into, pour into. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): put on, wear, fasten. Other forms: vow, vownin. Gen 42:25

vo v. — fear, revere. Luke 12:5

vɔɛiyo v. — suck (at the breast); kiss; (noun) suckling. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): nurse (a baby), suck. Other forms: vɔɛi, vɔɛinin. Luke 7:38

vɔɛsio v. — breastfeed, nurse. Other forms: vɔɛsi, vɔɛsil. Exod 2:9

vɔkɔ-vɔkɔɔ n. — uproar, commotion, din. Other forms: vɔkɔ-vɔkɔ, vɔkɔ-vɔkɔlan. Acts 19:29

vɔ̀lɛ́lan n. — folds, pens (for livestock). Other forms: vɔ̀lɛ́la. Num 32:16

vɔlɔɔ n. (o) — partridge. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): bush chicken. 1 Sam 26:20

vɔlɔtɔɔ n. (o), pl. vɔlɔtɔlan — sickle. Other forms: vɔlɔtɔ. Deut 23:26

vɔmndo v. — beat (for game), hunt down. Other forms: vɔm. Hos 5:8

vɔngoo n. (o) — price, payment. Other forms: vɔngu. Gen 23:11

vɔ̀ngɔ̀ n. — reward, wages. Gen 15:1

vɔɔca v. — knead, mix (flour with oil); (vɔɔcan) mixed. Other forms: vɔɔcan. Num 15:6

vɔɔciaa v. — crush, dash to pieces. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): squeeze; arrange. Other forms: vɔɔciaanin. 2 Sam 22:39

vɔɔlen n. (len) — dry season. Gen 8:22

vɔɔndo1 adj. — bad, evil, wicked. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): bad, evil; also ugly (wɔ̀ùwó 'be bad or ugly'). Other forms: vɔɔn, vɔɔnda, vɔɔnnda, vɔɔnndan, vɔɔnndon, vɔɔnde, vɔɔnnden. Gen 2:9

vɔɔndo2 n. (o) — armpit. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): armpit; bosom. Gen 2:9

vɔɔsuuo v. — wipe, wipe away, blot out; forgive (sins); trim (lamps). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): wipe off, clean, erase; brush off, rub. Other forms: vɔɔsuu, vɔɔsuunin, vɔɔsu, vɔɔsun. Exod 30:7

vɔsio n. (o), pl. vɔsilan — year. Gen 1:14

vɔsɔkɔɔ n. — stony ground, rocky soil. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): gravel; gravelly upland soils. Mark 4:5

vɔwlen n. (len) — ugliness, badness; worse. Other forms: vɔwle. Gen 41:19

vɔw v. — be bad, be ugly; be severe. Other forms: vɔwnin. Exod 9:24

vɔyɔn ideo. — (sit on the ground) dejectedly, slumped. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): describes relaxing or sitting. Isa 47:1

vɔ́yɔ́ɔ́ n. — leftovers, remainder (of food). Ruth 2:14

vɔ part. — not yet (vɔ … le). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): also 'still, already'. Gen 2:5

vueinɔnndo v. — frighten, terrify; be fearsome. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): be afraid (middle of 'fear'); variant wèènɔ̌ŋndó, also 'frighten people'. Other forms: vueinun, vueinunnin, vueinɔn. 1 Chr 12:9

vuɛɛndo n. (o) — woman; (vocative) woman!. Other forms: vuɛɛn. John 8:10

vuilen n. (len) — theft, stealing. Exod 22:1

vuiyo n. (o), pl. vuiya — thief. Exod 22:1

vukɔɔ n. (o) — village meeting place for settling disputes. Keita 1979, p. 142

vulan n. — knees. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): knee (singular, le class). Ezek 47:4

vulen n. (len), pl. vulan — knee. Keita 1979, p. 133

vulɔɔ v. — grow, sprout. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): also: thread a needle. Other forms: vul, vulnin. Gen 3:18

vum ideo. — (ideophone) suddenly, with a start (pounding heart, fire flaring up). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): sound of slow regular beating (heartbeat), of a fire being lit. Gen 27:33

vunduan n. (an) — shade, shadows (plural of vundulen). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): plural (ma) of 'shade, shadow'; also the soul, an umbrella, an illustration. Other forms: vunduma. Judg 9:15

vundulen n. (len) — shadow, shade; vision. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): shade, shadow; the soul of a person. Gen 15:1

vuo v. — die. Other forms: vu, vunin, vi, vinin. Gen 43:8

vuulu v. — throw (something) to (someone). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): throw to someone; shoot, thatch for someone. 2 Sam 20:21

vuuo v. — throw, cast. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): throw (e.g. with a sling); thatch a roof; shoot. Other forms: vuu. Exod 4:3

wéé-wéé ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (cutting into small pieces). Childs 2000, p. 382

wèèyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — seeds for the warri game; the game itself. Childs 2000, p. 384

wèlèwèléí n. (i) — Southern Kissi only — dry branch. Childs 2000, p. 384

wémtú-wémtú ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (flat and thin: leaf, paper, hammered iron). Childs 2000, p. 384

wé ideo. — Southern Kissi only — bit by bit, piece by piece. Childs 2000, p. 383

wílé ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (very cold: water, wind, rain). Childs 2000, p. 385

wìòmɔ̀ɔ́ n. (o), pl. wìòmɔ̀ɔ̀láŋ — Southern Kissi only — errand. Childs 2000, p. 387

wòlìtánàá n. (i) — Southern Kissi only — tree species used to make doors. Childs 2000, p. 388

wòlú-wòlú ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (flowing water). Childs 2000, p. 388

wóníwálí interj. — Southern Kissi only — congratulations, greeting to people at work. Childs 2000, p. 388

wóŋáá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — lower back. Childs 2000, p. 389

wóŋgbóŋ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — completely clear, open. Childs 2000, p. 389

wóŋóó n. (o), pl. wóŋúéí — Southern Kissi only — tree species, good firewood. Childs 2000, p. 389

wòùwó v. — Southern Kissi only — faint. Childs 2000, p. 390

wɔ̀kɔ̀lɔ̀ɔ́ n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — thatching grass. Childs 2000, p. 390

wɔ́pèlɛ̂ŋ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (describes encountering). Childs 2000, p. 391

wɔ̀wàá v. — Southern Kissi only — retch, vomit, heave. Childs 2000, p. 391

wɔ̂ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (sound of something heavy dropping). Childs 2000, p. 390

wûlé-wûlé ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (blaze of dry cuttings burning). Childs 2000, p. 392

wúlùlù-wúlùlù ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (picking up in clumps or bunches). Childs 2000, p. 392

wûm-wùm ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (eating greedily). Childs 2000, p. 393

yaafalen n. (len) — betrayal. Keita 1979, p. 156

yaafanɔɔ n. (o) — traitor. Keita 1979, p. 156

yaalaa v. — condemn, accuse. Other forms: yaala. John 8:10

yaalanndo v. — condemn oneself. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): incriminate oneself. 1 Cor 11:29

yaalei n., pl. yaalelan — jaw, jawbone; (pl.) jaws, cheeks. Other forms: yaale, yaalela. Judg 15:15

yaalianndo v. — rebuke sharply, scold (to silence). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): frighten; shout to scare away birds; judge, find guilty. Matt 20:31

yààmàá v. — Southern Kissi only — yawn; wheeze. Childs 2000, p. 394

yaamɔɔlen n. (len) — enmity, hostility, hatred. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): hatred, jealousy. Eph 2:14

yaamɔɔ n. (o), pl. yaamɔaa — enemy. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): enemy, someone hated. Exod 23:4

yáánáná ideo. — Southern Kissi only — weak, listless, downcast. Childs 2000, p. 395

yàándɔɔ num. — third. Other forms: yàándɔlen, yàándɔ. Gen 14:4

yáásàá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — plant species with edible leaves. Childs 2000, p. 395

yààwèí n. (i), pl. yààwǎŋ — Southern Kissi only — onion. Childs 2000, p. 396

yààyàá2 v. — Southern Kissi only — augment, amplify (a case); celebrate (returning initiates). Childs 2000, p. 396

yààyɛ́í n. (i), pl. yààyáŋ — Southern Kissi only — bells, iron rattles, strung small bells. Childs 2000, p. 396

yàá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — snake species. Childs 2000, p. 394

yáá num. — three. Gen 2:19

yabibio n. (o) — pineapple. Keita 1979, p. 140

yákólàá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — large monkey. Childs 2000, p. 396

yalaa n. (o), pl. yalalan — net. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): round scoop net used by women for fishing; mosquito net. Ps 25:15

docs.title: Glossary of grammatical terms
docs.text:
Terms used in this guide, with their French equivalent.

Term French Definition agreement accord Repetition of a noun's class on the words that accompany it. See Agreement. benefactive bénéfactif Derived verb showing that the action is done for someone: dimul “say to”. causative causatif Derived verb meaning “make do, make be”: hivia “make pass”. circumposition circumposition Preposition and postposition framing a noun: o … nin “in”. class pronoun pronom de classe Pronoun that refers back to a noun according to its class: le, la, ma. class referent référent de classe Class suffix repeated at the end of a relative clause: fula-o. class suffix terminaison de classe End of the noun that shows its class and number: -ndo, -lan, -len… full form forme pleine Noun with its class suffix: cɛiyo. habitual habituel Aspect of habitual or general action. ideophone idéophone Expressive word that depicts a sound or a manner: púŋ, few-few. long form, verbal noun forme longue Form of the verb ending like a noun (tosaa), used after co, va. long vowel voyelle longue Vowel pronounced for longer, written double: aa, ɔɔ. middle moyen Derived verb with a reflexive or passive meaning: cɔmnun “show oneself”. noun class classe nominale Group of nouns that have the same suffix and the same agreements. See Noun classes. particle particule Small invariable word with a grammatical function: ni, le, yɛ. perfective accompli Aspect that presents the action as completed: I tuei “I have heard”. postposition postposition Relational word placed after the noun: coo “on”, nin “in”. progressive progressif Aspect of action in progress: co / va + long form. relative clause relative Clause that modifies a noun: lɔma ya sɔl-lan “the dream that I had”. stem radical Part of the word that carries the meaning, without a suffix. stem form forme radicale Noun without a suffix, before a determiner: cɛi kon. subjunctive subjonctif Mood of purpose and wish: mò + verb. tone ton Pitch of the voice on a syllable, which can change the meaning. See Tone.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
• Verb tables: the forms of regular and irregular verbs and of the verb “be”;
  • Kisiei–English dictionary: the whole lexicon in alphabetical order;
  • English–Kisiei index: find a Kisiei word from English;
  • Word lists: the same vocabulary arranged by field of meaning;
  • Common phrases: greeting, thanking, answering, asking for information;
  • Glossary: the grammatical terms used in this guide;
  • Open questions: points to be checked with speakers.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text: These points cannot be settled from the written sources alone: the Bible (BKG) does not mark everything (in particular tones), the 1979 description (Keita 1979) is sometimes incomplete or contradicted by the Bible, and Childs's description (Childs 1995) concerns Southern Kissi. They are put to speakers and teachers; all observations are welcome (see the project repository).

docs.title: Spelling
docs.text:
1. Tones. Which tones should be marked, apart from the grammatical cases where the Bible marks them regularly (mí / mì, háá, ndóò, tùú)? The lexical tones of common words are not described anywhere for the Kisiei of Guinea. See Tone.
  2. Alphabetical order. The order proposed in this guide for ɛ, ɔ, ŋ, ɲ and the digraphs needs to be validated. See Alphabet.
  3. Words not in the Bible. The respelled 1979 forms (status Respelled) must be confirmed one by one, in particular vowel length and the final nasal (n or ŋ).

docs.title: Nouns and determiners
docs.text:
1. Near and far in the an, len, lan classes. According to the 1979 description, man, len, lan are used for “this…” and “that…”, distinguished by tone (Keita 1979, p. 58). To be checked.
  2. Irregular plurals. The 1979 list of irregular plurals (Keita 1979, p. 26-29) needs to be completed and checked.
  3. 1st and 2nd person plural possessives for the i and -on classes: forms not found in the Bible.
  4. 1979 indefinites kèkè “any” and yööli “all”, not found in the Bible: do they still exist, and how should they be written?
  5. 1979 interrogatives köè and ngö “which”, not found in the Bible.
  6. Negating a noun. In Southern Kissi, the negated noun in “it is not X” takes its class pronoun (Childs 1995, p. 261-262). Is this the case in the Kisiei of Guinea?

docs.title: Verb
docs.text:
1. Tone of the perfective and the habitual. These two forms differ only in tone (Keita 1979, p. 95); a precise description of verbal tones is lacking.
  2. Stems of “go”. The Bible uses kɔa in narrative and kɔɛ after mì; the 1979 description gives köè in the past and köa in the habitual. Which of the two distributions is that of everyday usage?
  3. The particle -lɔ / -ndɔ / -yɔ. Its use for politeness is clear (yaŋ-ndɔ), but the Bible also uses it in negative sentences in the past (ndóò vil-lɔ … le Gen 2:5). What is this second use?
  4. Reciprocal. The 1979 description gives long forms -anndo, -lanndo (yilanndo), not found in the Bible.
  5. Future with co and future with -nin. What difference in meaning do speakers make between n co ndu dio and dianin?

docs.title: Varieties
docs.text: 1. Regional variants. The handwritten notes mention Kissidougou variants (r for l, other words). Which of them should be part of a common written usage? See Regional varieties.

docs.title: Common phrases
docs.text: A few common phrases, all taken from the Kisiei Bible (BKG). They show the spelling and the construction; in conversation, polite formulas may vary from region to region.

docs.title: Greeting, thanking, asking
docs.text: Kisiei English Reference Pua isɛ Greetings, father. Gen 27:18 Mbaa Yes? (answer to someone calling) Gen 27:18 A yandi Please, I beg you. Gen 14:21 balika thank you Gen 24:48 Hala dɔw nɔm duaa May God bless you. Luke 1:42

docs.title: Answering
docs.text: Kisiei English Reference Oi Yes. Gen 24:58 Ɛ-ɛ No. Gen 3:2 I sínà le I don't know. 1 Sam 17:55 O co kɛndɛ He is well. Gen 29:6

docs.title: Introducing oneself, asking for information
docs.text:
Kisiei English Reference Nɔm nɛ̀ɛ́-nɛ̀? Who are you? Gen 27:32 Ya Esau ni I am Esau. Gen 27:32 Kuɛɛ niaa fula yɛ? Where do you come from? Gen 29:4 Haran naa n fula ni We come from Haran. Gen 29:4 Vɛ̀ɛ̀ o co kɛndɛ lon? Is he well? Gen 29:6 Kuɛɛ nɛ n co yɛ? Where are you? Gen 3:9

For other everyday greetings, see the dialogues in the 1979 description (in the old spelling) (Keita 1979); forms that do not appear in the Bible must be checked with speakers.

docs.title: Verb tables
docs.text: These tables summarise the forms described on the pages Stems and groups, Tense, aspect and mood and Negation, generally with the pronoun o “he, she”. All the combinations given are attested in the Kisiei Bible (BKG); tone, which is not marked, distinguishes some forms that are identical in writing.

Note

The 1979 description gives complete tables for sixteen verbs, with all six persons (Keita 1979, p. 96-109), in the old spelling; the description of Southern Kissi gives the paradigms of cimbu “leave” and kiol “bite” (Childs 1995, p. 220-221). The tables above keep only the forms checked in the Bible.

docs.title: Word lists
docs.text: These lists are generated automatically from the project's lexicon (4250 entries). Words are grouped by semantic domain following the SIL Semantic Domains classification; a word may appear in several domains. Attested words link to their first occurrence in the Kisiei Bible; Confirmed words are not in the Bible but confirmed by a speaker; Respelled words come from the 1979 description and still need confirmation; Southern Kissi words are known only from the Southern Kissi dictionary (Childs 2000): they are not attested in the North and are spelled as Childs writes them. The lexicon is also available as CSV, TSV, LIFT (for FieldWorks) and CLDF.

docs.title: Archive
docs.text: The archive/ folder of the repository keeps older documents on Kisiei: those on which this guide is based, and other sources (word lists, texts, lists of terms) still to be used. Most are scanned typescripts that predate the current spelling: they are not a spelling model, and anything taken from them is checked against the Bible.

docs.title: Sékou Sondo Keita and the Académie des langues
docs.text: Document Contents Kissie fondamental (scan) Scan (189 pages) of Sékou Sondo Keita's thesis, Essai d'élaboration d'un kisiei fondamental à l'usage des locuteurs non kisi, Institut polytechnique Gamal Abdel Nasser de Conakry, 1979. Kissie fondamental (transcription) Full transcription in Markdown, in the original spelling; the handwritten corrections are incorporated. This transcription is final and will not be converted to the current spelling. Kissie fondamental (handwritten notes) Handwritten annotations by later readers, page by page: translations, French glosses, Kissidougou variants (Annotations manuscrites portées sur l'exemplaire numérisé de Keita (1979) s.d.). Kissie fondamental (annex) The thesis annex, Contes, proverbes, devinettes (typescript pp. 166–184), found separately and missing from the main scan: 18 pages of Kisiei tales, each followed by proverbs (talelan) and riddles (budon pialan), with handwritten French glosses (Keita 1979). Not transcribed. Terminology: language, arts, history, ideology Four lists from the Académie des langues (Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research): numbered French terms with their Kisiei translation, for language and grammar (16 pp.), the arts (12 pp.), history and politics (21 pp.), ideology, economy and society (13 pp.) (Académie des Langues s.d.). The pages name no author; the attribution to Keita comes from the file names. Nouvelle orthographe kissi Correspondence sheet between the old and the new spelling (Nouvelle orthographe kissi (tableau de correspondances) s.d.).

docs.title: Denise Paulme
docs.text: Document Contents Documents sur la langue kissi Documents sur la langue kissi : lexique et textes (Paulme 1964), 173 pages, printed from the University of Florida Digital Collections. Vocabulary and texts collected by the ethnologist Denise Paulme during two stays in the Kissi country with André Schaeffner (October 1945 – June 1946, October 1948 – May 1949), around Kissidougou and Guéckédou; with a bibliography of earlier work on Kissi. Kissi vocabulaire Another copy of the same work (151 pages), scanned from a typescript, with a few handwritten notes.

docs.title: Other documents
docs.text: Document Contents Lexique kissi – français Alphabetical Kisiei–French word list of 68 pages, author unknown, typed in the current spelling (ɛ, ɔ), with handwritten additions (Lexique kissi – français s.d.).

docs.title: How to cite the 1979 manual
docs.text:
The page numbers cited (“Keita 1979, p. 57”) are those of the typescript. In the transcription, each page begins with a link to the handwritten notes for that page (“✎ Handwritten notes, p. 57”), which makes it easy to find the passage.

The spelling of quotations from 1979 is that of the original (tyo, nh, è, ö…); the Old and new spelling page explains how to read it.

docs.title: Bibliography

The references cited in the guide, in alphabetical order of author. Citations such as “(Keita 1979, p. 57)” refer to this list; Bible references (“Gen 1:3”) link to the corresponding verse of the Kisiei Bible on bible.com.

The works of the Académie des Langues and the theses of the Institut polytechnique de Conakry cited in 1979 (Tolno, Sow, Kamano, Camara, Iffono) could not be consulted; they are given as listed in the bibliography of Keita (1979).

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
This guide relies on three sets of sources, in this order of authority:

  1. The Kisiei Bible (BKG), the standard for spelling and usage;
  2. Keita's manual (Keita 1979) and its handwritten annotations, the basic description of the grammar;
  3. Childs's grammar and dictionary (Childs 1995, 2000), a description of Southern Kissi, for comparison.

The Sources and the standard page explains this choice.

  • Bibliography: all the references cited;
  • Archive: the documents kept in the repository;
  • Tools: the list of Bible words, the concordance and the automatic checks.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text: The rules of this guide are drawn from the texts of the Kisiei Bible (BKG) with the help of a few tools, available in the tools/ folder of the repository. They are run with uv.

docs.title: The Bible text
docs.text:
tools/fetch_bible.py downloads the chapters of the Kisiei Bible from bible.com, slowly (about one per second), into a local .cache/bible/ folder that is not added to the repository: the text remains the property of the Alliance Biblique en Guinée. Only the list of word forms is published.

uv run tools/fetch_bible.py --delay 1.0

docs.title: The list of word forms
docs.text: tools/build_wordlist.py produces references/bible-bkg-wordforms.tsv: each word form of the Bible (ignoring tones and capitals), its number of occurrences, its spellings with tone accents and a first reference. The complete Bible (1,188 chapters) contains about 939,000 words and nearly 22,000 different forms.

docs.title: The concordance
docs.text:
tools/bible_concordance.py searches the local text for a word, part of a word or a pattern, and shows each occurrence in its context with its reference. It is the main tool for checking a rule:

uv run tools/bible_concordance.py -w "ndɔ(ɔ|a|lan|len)"

docs.title: The automatic checks
docs.text:
Every time the site is built (mkdocs build --strict), a module (tools/kisiei_hooks.py):

  • checks that every Kisiei example marked as attested is in the list of Bible word forms; otherwise, the build fails;
  • turns citations (“(Keita 1979, p. 57)”) into links to the bibliography and reports unknown keys;
  • also accepts an abbreviation in double square brackets (book code, chapter and verse, for example GEN.1.3) for a Bible reference, but the pages write references as plain Markdown links to the verse on bible.com ([Gen 1:3](https://www.bible.com/bible/1394/GEN.1.3.BKG)), which are also readable outside the site.

tools/check_i18n.py checks that every page exists in French and in English.
